title.raw: 卷21下 獻文六王下 Volume 21b: Emperor Xianwen's Six Princes 2

sentences.zh: 彭城王

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pengcheng

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰，字彥和。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie, style Yanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Xie, Prince of Pengcheng, styled Yanhe.

sentences.zh: 少而歧嶷，姿性不羣。

translations.literal: From youth precocious and sharp; his bearing and nature were not of the common sort.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was precocious and sharp; in bearing and temperament he stood apart.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，封始平王，加侍中、征西大將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Shiping and made Palace Attendant and General Who Conquers the West.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 9 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shiping and made palace attendant and general who conquers the west.

sentences.zh: 勰生而母潘氏卒，其年顯祖崩。

translations.literal: When Xie was born his mother Lady Pan died; that same year Xianwen passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was born the year his mother Lady Pan died; that same year Xianwen passed away.

sentences.zh: 及有所知，啟求追服。

translations.literal: When he came to understanding he petitioned to observe mourning for her.
translations.idiomatic: Once he could understand, he petitioned to mourn her properly.

sentences.zh: 文明太后不許，乃毀瘠三年，弗參吉慶。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming would not permit it; he therefore wasted away three years and took no part in joyous celebrations.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming refused; he wasted away for three years and joined no festive occasion.

sentences.zh: 高祖大奇之。

translations.literal: Gaozu marvelled greatly at him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was deeply struck by him.

sentences.zh: 敏而耽學，不捨晝夜，博綜經史，雅好屬文。

translations.literal: Keen and addicted to study, never setting it aside day or night; broadly mastered classics and histories; elegantly fond of composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and devoted to books, he studied day and night without pause, mastered the classics and histories broadly, and loved to write.

sentences.zh: 高祖革創，解侍中、將軍，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was founding the realm, he was relieved of Palace Attendant and general and appointed Grand Master for the Glorious.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was still founding the realm, Xie was relieved of palace attendant and general and made grand master for the glorious.

sentences.zh: 復除侍中，長直禁內，參決軍國大政，萬機之事，無不預焉。

translations.literal: Again made Palace Attendant, on long duty within the forbidden interior, deliberating great affairs of army and state; of the myriad reins nothing was not his to share.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made palace attendant and kept long watch inside the palace, sharing in every great decision of army and state.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南伐，以勰行撫軍將軍，領宗子軍，宿衞左右。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Xie was made Acting General Who Pacifies the Army, commanding the army of imperial clansmen, guarding close at night.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Xie was made acting general who pacifies the army, took command of the clansmen's guard, and slept in attendance at his side.

sentences.zh: 開建五等，食邑二千戶，轉中書令，侍中如故，改封彭城王。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, fief of two thousand households; transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Palace Attendant as before; enfeoffment changed to Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the five ranks were instituted he received two thousand revenue households, became director of the secretariat while remaining palace attendant, and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖與侍臣昇金墉城，顧見堂後梧桐、竹曰：「鳳皇非梧桐不栖，非竹實不食，今梧桐、竹並茂，詎能降鳳乎？

translations.literal: Gaozu with attendant ministers ascended the Jinfeng city wall, looked back and saw behind the hall parasol trees and bamboo, and said: "The phoenix does not perch except on the parasol tree and does not eat except bamboo seeds; now parasol tree and bamboo both flourish—can a phoenix descend?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu climbed the Jinfeng wall with his attendants, glanced at the parasol trees and bamboo behind the hall, and said, "The phoenix perches only on the parasol tree and eats only bamboo seed. Both are lush now—will a phoenix come down?"

sentences.zh: 」勰對曰：「鳳皇應德而來，豈竹、梧桐能降？

translations.literal: " Xie replied: "The phoenix comes in response to virtue—how could parasol tree and bamboo bring it down?
translations.idiomatic: Xie answered, "The phoenix answers virtue. How could trees and bamboo summon it?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「何以言之？

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "By what do you say so?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked, "On what grounds?"

sentences.zh: 」勰曰：「昔在虞舜，鳳皇來儀；

translations.literal: " Xie said: "In the time of Shun of Yu the phoenix came with ceremony;
translations.idiomatic: Xie said, "Under Shun of Yu the phoenix came in ritual order;"

sentences.zh: 周之興也，鸑鷟鳴於岐山。

translations.literal: when Zhou rose, the luan and zhuo birds cried on Mount Qi.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhou rose, the luan and zhuo cried on Mount Qi.

sentences.zh: 未聞降桐食竹。

translations.literal: One has not heard of descending for parasol trees or eating bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: No one ever heard of a phoenix coming down for timber or bamboo alone.

sentences.zh: 」高祖笑曰：「朕亦未望降之也。

translations.literal: " Gaozu laughed and said: "I too have not hoped for a descent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed. "I never expected one either."

sentences.zh: 」後宴侍臣於清徽堂。

translations.literal: " Later he feasted the attendant ministers in the Clear Emblem Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later he feasted his attendants in the Clear Emblem Hall.

sentences.zh: 日晏，移於流化池芳林之下。

translations.literal: The day grew late; they moved to beneath the fragrant grove at the Transforming Flow Pool.
translations.idiomatic: As the day waned they moved to the fragrant grove by the Transforming Flow Pool.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「向宴之始，君臣肅然，及將末也，觴情始暢，而流景將頹，竟不盡適，戀戀餘光，故重引卿等。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "At the start of the earlier feast ruler and ministers were all solemn; toward the end the cups began to loosen and the flowing light was about to fall—yet we did not fully enjoy it, still lingering on the afterglow; therefore I have again summoned you.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "At first we were all stiff with ceremony; near the end the wine began to flow freely, yet the light was failing before we had our fill. I still hunger for that glow, so I have called you back."

sentences.zh: 」因仰觀桐葉之茂，曰：「『其桐其椅，其實離離，愷悌君子，莫不令儀』，今林下諸賢，足敷歌詠。

translations.literal: " He then looked up at the parasol leaves' lushness and said: "'Its parasol, its chair-tree, fruit hanging thick; a gracious prince—none without fine deportment.' Now the worthies beneath this grove are enough to fill a song.
translations.idiomatic: He looked up at the thick parasol leaves and quoted, "'Parasol and chair-tree, fruit hanging thick; gracious princes, none without fine bearing.' The men in this grove are fit for verse."

sentences.zh: 」遂令黃門侍郎崔光讀暮春羣臣應詔詩。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Guang to read the late-spring poems the ministers had composed on imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Guang to read the late-spring poems composed on imperial command.

sentences.zh: 至勰詩，高祖仍為之改一字，曰：「昔祁奚舉子，天下謂之至公，今見勰詩，始知中令之舉非私也。

translations.literal: When they came to Xie's poem Gaozu still altered one character for him and said: "In old times Qi Xi recommended his son and the realm called it utmost fairness; now seeing Xie's poem I know the Director of the Secretariat's recommendation was not private.
translations.idiomatic: At Xie's poem Gaozu changed one character himself and said, "When Qi Xi recommended his own son the realm called it perfect fairness. Your poem shows my secretariat director did not favor you privately."

sentences.zh: 」勰對曰：「臣露此拙，方見聖朝之私，賴蒙神筆賜刊，得有令譽。

translations.literal: " Xie replied: "Your subject exposed this clumsy work and thereby showed the holy court's favoritism; relying on the divine brush's correction I may have a fair reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xie replied, "By showing this clumsy verse I only exposed the court's partiality. Your brush's correction is what gives it any reputation at all."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「雖琢一字，猶是玉之本體。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "Though one character is carved away, it is still the jade's own body.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Even carved by a single character, it remains jade in substance."

sentences.zh: 」勰曰：「臣聞詩三百，一言可蔽。

translations.literal: " Xie said: "Your subject has heard that in the three hundred poems one phrase can sum them up.
translations.idiomatic: Xie said, "They say the three hundred poems may be summed in a single line."

sentences.zh: 今陛下賜刊一字，足以價等連城。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's gift of carving one character is enough to equal a linked city in price."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's one-character revision is worth a city of jade."

sentences.zh: 勰表解侍中，詔曰：「蟬貂之美，待汝而光，人乏之秋，何容方退也。

translations.literal: Xie memorialized to resign as Palace Attendant; an edict said: "The beauty of the cicada-fur cap awaits you to shine; in a season when men are lacking, how can you step back?
translations.idiomatic: Xie asked to resign as palace attendant. The edict read, "The court's dignity waits on you to shine. In a season when talent is scarce, how can you withdraw?"

sentences.zh: 克念作聖，庶必有資耳。

translations.literal: If you can think earnestly and become sage, there will surely be material for it.
translations.idiomatic: "If you set your mind to it, you will have much to give."

sentences.zh: 」後幸代都，次于上黨之銅鞮山。

translations.literal: " Later, when Gaozu favored the northern capital, they halted at Tongdi Mountain in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a journey to the northern capital, the court halted at Tongdi Mountain in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 路旁有大松樹十數根。

translations.literal: Beside the road were more than ten great pine trees.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten great pines stood beside the road.

sentences.zh: 時高祖進傘，遂行而賦詩，令人示勰曰：「吾始作此詩，雖不七步，亦不言遠。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu advanced under an umbrella and went on composing a poem, sending someone to show Xie and say: "I have just begun this poem; though not in seven paces, it is not far off either.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu walked on under his umbrella composing a poem and sent word to Xie: "I have just started this piece. It may not be seven paces, but it is not far off."

sentences.zh: 汝可作之，比至吾所，令就之也。

translations.literal: You may compose one; by the time you reach where I am, finish it there.
translations.idiomatic: "Compose one yourself and finish it by the time you reach me."

sentences.zh: 」時勰去帝十餘步，遂且行且作，未至帝所而就。

translations.literal: " At that time Xie was more than ten paces from the emperor; he therefore composed as he walked and finished before reaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was still ten paces behind; he wrote as he walked and finished before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 詩曰：「問松林，松林經幾冬？

translations.literal: The poem said: "I ask the pine grove—how many winters has the pine grove known?
translations.idiomatic: His poem ran: "I ask the pine grove—how many winters has it seen?"

sentences.zh: 山川何如昔，風雲與古同。

translations.literal: How are mountains and rivers unlike the past? Wind and clouds are the same as of old.
translations.idiomatic: "Are mountains and rivers unchanged? Wind and clouds are as they were of old."

sentences.zh: 」高祖大笑曰：「汝此詩亦調責吾耳。

translations.literal: " Gaozu laughed greatly and said: "Your poem also tunes its blame at me.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed aloud. "Your poem rebukes me as well."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「弟勰所生母潘早齡謝世，顯號未加，勰禍與身具，痛隨形起，今因其展思，有足悲矜，可贈彭城國太妃，以慰存亡。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Younger brother Xie's birth mother Lady Pan departed early in years; a splendid title was not yet added. Xie's grief was born with his body and pain rose with his form. Now, because he extends his thought, there is ample cause for pity; she may be posthumously enfeoffed Grand Consort of the Pengcheng state to comfort the living and the dead.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Younger brother Xie's mother Lady Pan died young without a posthumous title. His grief has been with him from birth. Moved by his devotion, posthumously enfeoff her as Grand Consort of Pengcheng to comfort living and dead alike."

sentences.zh: 」又除中書監，侍中如故。

translations.literal: " Again he was made Director of the Secretariat, Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made director of the secretariat while remaining palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖南討漢陽，假勰中軍大將軍，加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned south against Hanyang he made Xie acting Grand General of the Center Army and added one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu marched south against Hanyang he made Xie acting grand general of the center army and granted a set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 勰以寵受頻煩，乃面陳曰：「臣聞兼親疏而兩，並異同而建，此既成文於昔，臣願誦之於後。

translations.literal: Because favors came in quick succession Xie spoke to his face and said: "Your subject has heard that joining near and far in one post and establishing different and same together—this was already written in the past; your subject wishes to recite it for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Favored again and again, Xie spoke plainly: "I have heard that to join near and far in one office and to set unlike with alike was written long ago. I wish to recite it for what comes after."

sentences.zh: 陳思求而不允，愚臣不請而得。

translations.literal: Chen Si sought and was not granted; this foolish subject did not seek yet obtained.
translations.idiomatic: "Chen Si asked and was refused; I did not ask and was given."

sentences.zh: 豈但今古云殊，遇否大異，非獨曹植遠羨於臣，是亦陛下踐魏文而不顧。

translations.literal: How could it be only that past and present differ in saying so—the encounter of fortune and misfortune differs greatly; it is not only that Cao Zhi from afar envies your subject—it is also that Your Majesty treads where Emperor Wen of Wei would not look.
translations.idiomatic: "Past and present are not the only divide—fortune and misfortune differ as well. It is not only that Cao Zhi envies me from afar; Your Majesty walks where Emperor Wen of Wei would not tread."

sentences.zh: 」高祖大笑，執勰手曰：「二曹才名相忌，吾與汝以道德相親，緣此而言，無慚前烈。

translations.literal: " Gaozu laughed greatly, took Xie's hand and said: "The two Caos envied each other's talent and fame; I and you are kin by virtue. On this account I need not blush before the former exemplars.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed and took his hand. "The two Caos were jealous of each other's gifts; you and I are joined by virtue. On that score I need not blush before the ancients."

sentences.zh: 汝但克己復禮，更何多及。」

translations.literal: You need only restrain yourself and return to ritual—what more is needed?"
translations.idiomatic: "Only restrain yourself and return to ritual. What more is there?"

sentences.zh: 高祖親講喪服於清徽堂，從容謂羣臣曰：「彥和、季豫等年在蒙稚，早登纓紱，失過庭之訓，並未習禮，每欲令我一解喪服。

translations.literal: Gaozu personally lectured on mourning garments in the Clear Emblem Hall and said at ease to the assembled ministers: "Yanhe, Jiyu and the others are still in tender years; they early donned the cap and sash; they lost the training of the courtyard and have not yet learned ritual; I have often wished to have them understand mourning garments once from me.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu lectured on mourning dress in the Clear Emblem Hall and told the ministers at ease, "Yanhe, Jiyu, and the others are still young. They took cap and sash early, missed the courtyard's instruction, and do not yet know ritual. I have often wished to explain mourning dress to them myself."

sentences.zh: 自審義解浮疏，抑而不許。

translations.literal: On examining myself my understanding is thin and floating; I therefore suppressed it and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: "Reviewing my own understanding, I found it shallow and held back."

sentences.zh: 頃因酒醉坐，脫爾言從，故屈朝彥，遂親傳說。

translations.literal: Recently, because I was sitting drunk, I suddenly assented; therefore I have bent the court's worthies and now personally transmit the explanation.
translations.idiomatic: "Lately, drunk in my seat, I assented without thinking, and so I have bent the court's worthies to hear me teach it now."

sentences.zh: 將臨講坐，慚戰交情。

translations.literal: As I am about to take the lecturing seat I am ashamed and my feelings tremble.
translations.idiomatic: "As I take the teacher's seat I am ashamed and my heart trembles."

sentences.zh: 」御史中尉李彪對曰：「自古及今，未有天子講禮。

translations.literal: " Imperial Censor Zhongwei Li Biao replied: "From antiquity until now there has never been a Son of Heaven who lectured on ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial censor Li Biao answered, "From antiquity until now no Son of Heaven has lectured on ritual."

sentences.zh: 陛下聖叡淵明，事超百代，臣得親承音旨，千載一時。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sagacity and perspicacity surpass a hundred generations; your subject obtains the honor of receiving the tone in person—a moment once in a thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty's sagacity surpasses a hundred generations. To receive your teaching in person is a moment that comes once in a thousand years."

sentences.zh: 從征沔北，賜帛三千匹。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign against the Mian he was given three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign north of the Mian he was given three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 除使持節、都督南征諸軍事、中軍大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of All Armies on the Southern Expedition, Grand General of the Center Army, and Opener of the Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made bearer of the staff, commander of all armies on the southern expedition, grand general of the center army, and opener of the office.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「明便交敵，可敕將士肅爾軍儀。

translations.literal: Again an edict said: "Tomorrow we will meet the enemy; you may order the officers and soldiers to make their army bearing solemn.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added, "Tomorrow we engage the enemy. Order the troops to dress their ranks."

sentences.zh: 」勰於是親勒大眾。

translations.literal: " Xie thereupon personally drilled the great host.
translations.idiomatic: Xie personally drilled the great host.

sentences.zh: 須臾，有二大鳥從南而來，一向行宮，一向府幕，各為人所獲。

translations.literal: In a moment two great birds came from the south; one toward the traveling palace, one toward the command tent; each was caught by men.
translations.idiomatic: Soon two great birds flew from the south—one toward the traveling palace, one toward headquarters—and each was caught.

sentences.zh: 勰言於高祖曰：「始有一鳥，望旗顛仆，臣謂大吉。

translations.literal: Xie said to Gaozu: "At first one bird, seeing the banners, fell headlong; your subject called it great good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Xie told Gaozu, "Earlier one bird fell before our banners. I called that great fortune."

sentences.zh: 」高祖戲之曰：「鳥之畏威，豈獨中軍之略也，吾亦分其一爾。

translations.literal: " Gaozu jested with him: "Birds fear authority—is it only the center army's stratagem? I too share a portion.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu teased him, "Birds fear majesty—is that only your stratagem? I claim a share."

sentences.zh: 此乃大善，兵法咸說。

translations.literal: This is moreover great good; and all the military texts say so.
translations.idiomatic: "This is great good fortune, and every military classic says so."

sentences.zh: 」至明，便大破崔慧景、蕭衍。

translations.literal: " At dawn they utterly defeated Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they shattered Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 其夜大雨，高祖曰：「昔聞國軍獲勝，每逢雲雨。

translations.literal: That night came great rain; Gaozu said: "In old times one heard that when the state's army won, clouds and rain always followed.
translations.idiomatic: That night a great rain fell. Gaozu said, "They say that when the state's army wins, clouds and rain follow."

sentences.zh: 今破新野、南陽及摧此賊，果降時潤。

translations.literal: Now having taken Xinye and Nanyang and broken this bandit, timely moisture has indeed descended.
translations.idiomatic: "Having taken Xinye and Nanyang and broken this enemy, timely rain has come as promised."

sentences.zh: 誠哉斯言。

translations.literal: Truly this saying.
translations.idiomatic: "The saying is true."

sentences.zh: 」勰對曰：「水德之應，遠稱天心。

translations.literal: " Xie replied: "The response of the water virtue has long been called the heart of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Xie answered, "The response of water's virtue has long been called Heaven's own mind."

sentences.zh: 」高祖令勰為露布，勰辭曰：「臣聞露布者，布於四海，露之耳目，必須宣揚威略，以示天下。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered Xie to compose a victory bulletin; Xie declined and said: "Your subject has heard that a victory bulletin is spread to the four seas and exposed to all ears; it must proclaim martial prestige to show the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered Xie to draft the victory bulletin. Xie declined: "A victory bulletin is spread to the four seas and shown to every ear. It must proclaim our martial prestige to the world."

sentences.zh: 臣小才，豈足大用。

translations.literal: Your subject's small talent is not enough for great use.
translations.idiomatic: "My small talent is not fit for so great a use."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「汝豈獨親詔，亦為才達，但可為之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "You are not only close by imperial command—you are also accomplished in talent; only compose it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "You are not only my kin by decree—you are accomplished. Write it."

sentences.zh: 」及就，尤類帝文，有人見者，咸謂御筆。

translations.literal: " When it was done it especially resembled the emperor's own writing; those who saw it all said it was the imperial brush.
translations.idiomatic: When it was done it read like the emperor's own hand; all who saw it took it for his writing.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「汝所為者，人謂吾製，非兄則弟，誰能辨之。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "What you composed people say I made; if not elder brother then younger brother—who can tell?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "People say I wrote what you wrote. Between brothers, who can tell?"

sentences.zh: 」勰對曰：「子夏被蚩於先聖，臣又荷責於來今。」

translations.literal: " Xie replied: "Zixia was slandered before the sage; your subject again bears blame in the coming age."
translations.idiomatic: Xie answered, "Zixia was slandered before the sage; I again bear blame for the age to come."

sentences.zh: 及至豫州，高祖為家人書於勰曰：「教風密微，禮政嚴嚴，若不深心日勸，何以敬諸。

translations.literal: When they reached Yuzhou Gaozu wrote a family letter to Xie saying: "Teaching the wind is minute and close; ritual and government are stern and strict—if one does not with deep heart daily urge, how can one honor them?
translations.idiomatic: At Yuzhou Gaozu wrote Xie a family letter: "Teaching and custom are subtle; ritual and government are strict. Without daily urging from the heart, how can they be honored?"

sentences.zh: 每欲立一宗師，肅我元族。

translations.literal: I have often wished to establish one clan master to make solemn our primal clan.
translations.idiomatic: "I have long wished to set one master over the clan to make our house solemn."

sentences.zh: 汝親則宸極，位乃中監，風標才器，實足師範。

translations.literal: You are kin at the pole star's height and stand as Director at the Center; in bearing and talent you are truly fit to be a model.
translations.idiomatic: "You are kin at the throne's height and stand as director at the center. In bearing and talent you are truly fit to be the model."

sentences.zh: 屢有口敕，仍執沖遜，難違清挹，荏苒至今。

translations.literal: Repeated oral commands you still held in modest refusal; hard to go against pure restraint—time has slipped until now.
translations.idiomatic: "I have commanded you again and again, yet you still refuse in modesty. I could not override your restraint, and time has slipped by."

sentences.zh: 宗制之重，捨汝誰寄？

translations.literal: The weight of clan regulation—on whom else can it be laid?
translations.idiomatic: "The weight of clan law—on whom else can I lay it?"

sentences.zh: 便委以宗儀，責成汝躬，有不遵教典，隨事以聞，吾別肅治之。

translations.literal: Henceforth entrust clan ritual to you; let the charge be fulfilled on your person; where teaching and canon are not followed, report each matter as it arises and I will separately make it solemn.
translations.idiomatic: "Entrust clan ritual to you and let the charge rest on you. Where teaching is not followed, report each case and I will correct it."

sentences.zh: 若宗室有愆，隱而不舉，鍾罰汝躬。

translations.literal: If among the imperial clan there is fault and it is concealed and not reported, the bell punishment falls on your person.
translations.idiomatic: "If any in the clan offends and you conceal it, the penalty falls on you."

sentences.zh: 綱維相厲，庶有勸改。

translations.literal: Net and warp mutually urging—perhaps there will be urging to reform.
translations.idiomatic: "Let the net and the warp urge one another—perhaps there will be reform."

sentences.zh: 吾朝聞夕逝，不為恨也。

translations.literal: I hear in the morning and die at evening—there is no regret in that.
translations.idiomatic: "If I hear at dawn and die at dusk, I shall not regret it."

sentences.zh: 」勰翌日面陳曰：「奉詔令專主宗制，糾舉非違。

translations.literal: " The next day Xie spoke to his face and said: "Receiving the command to specialize in clan regulation and to investigate what violates it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xie spoke plainly: "I have received command to oversee clan regulation and investigate violations."

sentences.zh: 臣聞『其身正不令而行，其身不正雖令不從』。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: 'When the person is upright, orders proceed without being issued; when the person is not upright, though orders are issued they are not followed.'
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard: when the person is upright, orders run without being given; when the person is crooked, orders are given yet not followed."

sentences.zh: 臣處宗乏長幼之順，接物無國士之禮，每因啟請，已蒙哀借。

translations.literal: Your subject, placed among the clan, lacks the obedience of elder and younger; in receiving others lacks the ritual of a state's scholar; each time on petition I have already received compassionate indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: "Among the clan I lack proper deference between elder and younger; in dealing with others I lack a statesman's ritual. Each time I have petitioned you have indulged me."

sentences.zh: 不謂今詔，終不矜免。

translations.literal: I did not expect that in this present command there would in the end be no sparing.
translations.idiomatic: "I did not expect this command to spare me in the end."

sentences.zh: 猶願聖慈，賜垂蠲遂。

translations.literal: I still hope for sage compassion and a grant of release and completion.
translations.idiomatic: "I still beg your compassion to release me and let the charge be complete elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「汝諧，往欽哉。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "You are harmonious—go and revere it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "You are fit—go and honor the charge."

sentences.zh: 」勰表以一歲國秩、職俸、親恤以裨軍國，詔曰：「割身存國，理為遠矣。

translations.literal: " Xie memorialized to offer one year's state revenue, salary, and kin stipend to supplement army and state; an edict said: "Cutting the body to preserve the state—its principle is far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Xie memorialized to give one year's state revenue, salary, and kin stipend to the army and state. The edict read, "To cut from oneself to preserve the realm is principle of the farthest reach."

sentences.zh: 但汝以我親，[1]乃減己助國。

translations.literal: But because you are my kin, [1] you thereby reduced yourself to aid the state.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet because you are my kin,[1] you have reduced yourself to aid the state."

sentences.zh: 職俸便停，親、國二事，聽三分受一。」

translations.literal: Salary is stopped; for kin and state affairs, hear and receive one part in three."
translations.idiomatic: "Your salary is stopped; for kin and state obligations you may still receive one part in three."

sentences.zh: 高祖不豫，勰內侍醫藥，外總軍國之務，遐邇肅然，人無異議。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was unwell Xie attended within on medicine and without summed the affairs of army and state; far and near were solemn and none had a different opinion.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu fell ill Xie tended him within on medicine and without held army and state together; far and near were orderly and none disputed it.

sentences.zh: 徐謇當世之上醫也，先是，假還洛陽，及召至，勰引之別所，泣涕執手而謂之曰：「君今世元化，至尊氣力危惙，願君竭心，專思方治。

translations.literal: Xu Jie was the foremost physician of the age; earlier he had taken leave to return to Luoyang; when summoned and arrived Xie led him to a separate place, weeping and taking his hand, and said to him: "Sir, you are the age's primal transformer; the utmost venerable's breath and strength are critically weak; I wish you to exhaust your heart and think only on prescriptions and treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie was the age's finest physician. He had been on leave in Luoyang; when summoned, Xie led him aside, wept, took his hand, and said, "You are the age's great healer. The emperor's strength is critically weak. Exhaust your heart on his cure alone."

sentences.zh: 若聖體日康，令四海有賴，當獲意外之賞；

translations.literal: If the holy body daily grows healthy and thereby the four seas have reliance, you will obtain reward beyond expectation;
translations.idiomatic: "If he recovers and the realm has someone to rely on, you will receive reward beyond measure;"

sentences.zh: 不然，便有不測之誅，非但榮辱，乃存亡由此。

translations.literal: if not, then there will be punishment beyond reckoning—not only glory and shame but existence and extinction hang on this.
translations.idiomatic: "if not, punishment beyond reckoning—not only honor and shame but life and death hang on it."

sentences.zh: 君其勉之！

translations.literal: Sir, exert yourself!
translations.idiomatic: "Exert yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」左右見者，莫不嗚咽。

translations.literal: " Those at left and right who saw it all sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who witnessed it sobbed.

sentences.zh: 及引入，謇便欲進治。

translations.literal: When he was introduced Jie at once wished to advance treatment.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jie was brought in he wished to treat him at once.

sentences.zh: 勰以高祖神力虛弱，唯令以食味消息。

translations.literal: Because Gaozu's divine strength was weak Xie only ordered food flavors for restorative care.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gaozu's strength was feeble, Xie allowed only restorative food and gentle care.

sentences.zh: 勰乃密為壇於汝水之濱，依周公故事，告天地、顯祖請命，乞以身代。

translations.literal: Xie then secretly made an altar on the bank of the Ru River, following the Duke of Zhou's precedent, reporting to Heaven and Earth and Xianwen to request life, begging with his own body in substitution.
translations.idiomatic: Xie then secretly built an altar on the Ru's bank, following the Duke of Zhou's example, reporting to Heaven and Earth and Xianwen to beg for life, offering his own body in substitution.

sentences.zh: 高祖翊日有瘳損。

translations.literal: The day after Gaozu had some recovery.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Gaozu showed some improvement.

sentences.zh: 自懸瓠幸鄴，勰常侍坐輿輦，晝夜不離於側，飲食必先嘗之，而後手自進御。

translations.literal: From Xuanchi they favored Ye; Xie constantly attended beside the carriage day and night without leaving the side; he always tasted food and drink first and then with his own hand presented them to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: From Xuanchi the court favored Ye. Xie never left the carriage day or night, tasted every meal and drink first, and only then served the emperor with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，會百僚於宣極堂，行飲至策勳之禮。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital they met the hundred officials in the Hall of Proclaiming the Ultimate and performed the ritual of drinking to the end and recording merit.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital the court met the hundred officials in the Hall of Proclaiming the Ultimate and performed the rite of drinking to the end and recording merit.

sentences.zh: 命舍人宣旨：「勰翼弼六師，纂戎荊楚，沔北之勳，每毗廟算。

translations.literal: They ordered the palace attendant to proclaim the intent: "Xie assisted and supported the six armies, gathered the weapons in Jing-Chu; on the northern Mian his merit each time joined the temple's plans.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant proclaimed: "Xie assisted the six armies and gathered arms in Jing-Chu. North of the Mian his merit joined every plan of the temple."

sentences.zh: 從討新野，有克城之謀；

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Xinye he had the stratagem to take the city;
translations.idiomatic: "On the Xinye campaign he devised how to take the city;"

sentences.zh: 受命鄧城，致大捷之效。

translations.literal: receiving command at Dengcheng he achieved the effect of a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: "at Dengcheng he won the great victory."

sentences.zh: 功為羣將之最也。

translations.literal: His merit was foremost among the host of generals.
translations.idiomatic: "His merit stands first among the generals."

sentences.zh: 別當授賞，不替厥庸。

translations.literal: Separately he should receive reward without diminishing his service.
translations.idiomatic: "He shall be rewarded apart without diminishing his service."

sentences.zh: 」高祖謂勰曰：「吾與汝等，早罹艱苦，中逢契闊，每謂情義隨事而疏。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said to Xie: "I with you and the others early suffered hardship; in the middle we met separation; I have often said affection follows affairs and grows thin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told Xie, "You and I early knew hardship, then separation. I have often said affection thins with circumstance."

sentences.zh: 比纏患經歲，危如寒葉，非汝孔懷，情敦忠孝，孰能動止躬親，必先藥膳。

translations.literal: Recently, bound by illness for a year, perilous as a cold leaf—if not for your deep kin feeling and thick loyalty and filial piety, who could move and stop in person and first taste medicine and food?
translations.idiomatic: "Lately, a year in illness, perilous as a leaf in frost—without your deep kinship and loyal filial piety, who could attend in person, tasting medicine and food before me?"

sentences.zh: 每尋此事，感思殊遠。

translations.literal: Each time I trace this affair my moved thought is especially far.
translations.idiomatic: "Each time I recall it my gratitude goes very deep."

sentences.zh: 」勰悲泣對曰：「臣等宿遭不天，酷恨長世，賴陛下撫育，得參人伍。

translations.literal: " Xie wept and replied: "Your subjects long suffered an untimely heaven and bitterly resent a long lifetime; relying on Your Majesty's fostering we were able to join the ranks of men.
translations.idiomatic: Xie wept and answered, "We long suffered heaven's cruelty and bitterly resent long life. Only by Your Majesty's fostering did we join the ranks of men."

sentences.zh: 豈謂上靈無鑒，復使聖躬違和，萬國所懸，蒼生繫氣。

translations.literal: Who would have said the upper spirit had no mirror and again made the holy person depart from harmony—the ten thousand states hang on it, the dark masses tie their breath to it.
translations.idiomatic: "Who thought heaven had no mirror and would again make the holy person ill—the realm hangs on it, the people tie their breath to it."

sentences.zh: 寢興之勞，豈申荼蓼。

translations.literal: The labor of lying down and rising—how could it express bitter thoroughwort?
translations.idiomatic: "Our labor waking and sleeping cannot express our bitter thoroughwort."

sentences.zh: 」以破慧景等勳，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: " For merit in breaking Huijing and the others, fief increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For breaking Huijing and the rest his fief was increased by five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「朕形疲稚年，心勞長歲，積思成疴，頓發汝潁。

translations.literal: Again an edict said: "My form was weary from tender years and my heart labored through long years; accumulated thought became illness and suddenly broke out at Ru and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "My body was weary from youth and my heart labored through long years. Thought piled into illness and suddenly broke out at Ru and Ying."

sentences.zh: 第六弟勰，孝均周弟，感侔姬旦，遺食捨寐，動止必親，敦醫勸膳，誠力俱竭，致茲保康，實賴同氣。

translations.literal: The sixth younger brother Xie—filial piety equal to Zhou's younger brother, feeling comparable to the Duke of Zhou, leaving food and abandoning sleep, in movement and rest always in person, urging the physician and encouraging food—with loyal strength utterly spent he brought this preservation and health; truly it relied on shared breath.
translations.idiomatic: "My sixth brother Xie's filial piety matched Zhou's brother; his feeling matched the Duke of Zhou. He left food and sleep, was always in person, urged physicians and pressed food, spent himself utterly, and brought this recovery. It truly rested on shared breath."

sentences.zh: 又秉務緝政，百司是憑，綱維折衷，萬揆獲濟。

translations.literal: Again he held affairs and governed together; the hundred offices relied on him; net and warp weighed and balanced; the ten thousand measures obtained completion.
translations.idiomatic: "He also held government together; the hundred offices relied on him; he weighed the net and warp; the ten thousand measures were settled."

sentences.zh: 撫師於霖浩之辰，處戎於薦逼之日。

translations.literal: He pacified the armies in the season of great rain and handled arms on the day of repeated omens.
translations.idiomatic: "He pacified armies in seasons of flood and handled arms on days of ill omen."

sentences.zh: 安外靜內，功臣大道。

translations.literal: Securing the outer and quieting the inner—the great way of a meritorious minister.
translations.idiomatic: "Securing the outer and quieting the inner—that is a great minister's way."

sentences.zh: 侍省之績，可以孔懷無褒；

translations.literal: The achievement of attending and guarding within can make deep kin feeling without praise;
translations.idiomatic: "Attendance at the bedside needs no praise for deep kin feeling;"

sentences.zh: 翼亮之勤，實乃勳存社稷。

translations.literal: the diligence of assisting and brightening is truly merit that preserves altars and grain.
translations.idiomatic: "but assisting and brightening is merit that preserves the altars."

sentences.zh: 宜有酬賞，以旌國功，可增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: There should be recompense and reward to mark the state's merit; fief may increase by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: "There should be reward to mark the state's debt. Increase his fief by one thousand households."

sentences.zh: 」勰辭曰：「臣受遇緣親，榮枯事等，以此獲賞，殊乖情願，乞追成旨，用息謗言。

translations.literal: " Xie declined and said: "Your subject received encounter through kin; glory and withering are equal in the affair; to obtain reward on this account is especially contrary to feeling and wish; I beg to pursue and complete the former intent to still slander's words.
translations.idiomatic: Xie declined: "I was favored through kinship; glory and decline are one affair. Reward on this account goes against my wish. I beg to restore the former intent and still slander."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「汝在私能孝，處公必忠，比來勤憂，足布朝野，但可祗膺。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "You in private can be filial; in public you must be loyal; recently your diligent care is enough to spread through court and countryside—only reverently receive it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "In private you are filial; in public you are loyal. Your recent care fills court and countryside. Only receive it."

sentences.zh: 」尋以勰為司徒、太子太傅，侍中如故。

translations.literal: " Soon Xie was made Minister of Works and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made minister of works and grand tutor of the heir apparent while remaining palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 俄而蕭寶卷將陳顯達內寇，高祖復親討之。

translations.literal: Before long Xiao Baojuan was about to have Chen Xianda invade from within; Gaozu again personally campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiao Baojuan was to have Chen Xianda invade from within, and Gaozu again took the field in person.

sentences.zh: 詔勰使持節、都督中外諸軍事、總攝六師。

translations.literal: An edict made Xie Bearer of the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs Within and Without, and overall commander of the six armies.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was made bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs within and without, and overall commander of the six armies.

sentences.zh: 是時，高祖不豫。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was unwell.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then unwell.

sentences.zh: 勰辭曰：「臣侍疾無暇，六軍須有所託，事不兩興，情力又竭。

translations.literal: Xie declined and said: "Your subject attends illness without leisure; the six armies must have someone to rely on; the affair cannot rise in two places and feeling and strength are again exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Xie declined: "I attend his illness without rest. The six armies need another hand. Two burdens cannot rise together, and my strength is spent."

sentences.zh: 更請一王總當軍要。

translations.literal: I further request one prince to overall hold the military key.
translations.idiomatic: "I beg another prince to hold the military command."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「戎務、侍疾，皆憑於汝。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "Military affairs and attending illness both rely on you.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Military affairs and his sickbed both rest on you."

sentences.zh: 牽痾如此，吾深慮不濟。

translations.literal: Bound by illness like this—I deeply fear it will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: "Bound by illness as I am, I deeply fear I will not recover."

sentences.zh: 安六軍、保社稷者，捨汝而誰？

translations.literal: To secure the six armies and preserve altars and grain—apart from you, on whom?
translations.idiomatic: "To secure the six armies and preserve the realm—apart from you, whom?"

sentences.zh: 何容方便請人，以違心寄。

translations.literal: How can you for convenience request another person and thereby go against the heart's entrustment?
translations.idiomatic: "How can you for convenience ask another and betray what my heart entrusts?"

sentences.zh: 宗祏所賴，唯在於汝。

translations.literal: What the ancestral temple relies on is only in you.
translations.idiomatic: "The ancestral temple relies on you alone."

sentences.zh: 諸葛孔明、霍子孟異姓受託，而況汝乎！

translations.literal: Zhuge Kongming and Huo Zimeng, of different surname, received entrustment—how much more you!
translations.idiomatic: "Zhuge Kongming and Huo Zimeng were entrusted though of different surname—how much more you!"

sentences.zh: 」行次淯陽，高祖謂勰曰：「吾患轉惡，汝其努力。

translations.literal: " When they halted at Yuyang Gaozu said to Xie: "My illness turns worse; you must exert yourself.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuyang Gaozu told Xie, "My illness grows worse. Exert yourself."

sentences.zh: 」車駕至馬圈，去賊營數里，顯達等出戰，諸將大破之。

translations.literal: " When the imperial carriage reached Horse Pen, several li from the bandits' camp, Xianda and the others came out to battle and the generals utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Horse Pen, a few li from the enemy camp, Xianda came out to fight and the generals broke him utterly.

sentences.zh: 勰部分諸軍，將攻賊壘，其夜奔退。

translations.literal: Xie disposed the various armies and was about to attack the bandits' ramparts; that night they fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xie disposed the armies to storm the enemy ramparts; that night they fled.

sentences.zh: 高祖疾甚，謂勰曰：「修短命也，死生大分，今吾氣力危惙，當成不濟矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu's illness was severe; he said to Xie: "Xiu's life is short; death and life are a great division; now my breath and strength are critically weak and will surely not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's illness was grave. He told Xie, "Xiu's life is short; death and life are a great divide. My breath is failing and I will not recover."

sentences.zh: 雖敗顯達，國家安危，在此一舉，社稷所仗，唯在汝身。

translations.literal: Though Xianda is defeated, the state's safety and peril hang on this one throw; what the altars rely on is only in your person.
translations.idiomatic: "Though Xianda is beaten, the state's safety hangs on this one throw. The altars rely on you alone."

sentences.zh: 霍子孟以異姓受付，況汝親賢，可不勉也！

translations.literal: Huo Zimeng received charge though of different surname—how much more you, kin and worthy; can you not exert yourself!
translations.idiomatic: "Huo Zimeng took charge though of different surname—how much more you, kin and worthy. Exert yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」勰泣曰：「士於布衣，猶為知己盡命，況臣託靈先皇，聯暉陛下，誠應竭股肱之力，加之以忠貞。

translations.literal: " Xie wept and said: "A scholar in plain cloth still exhausts life for one who knows him; how much more your subject, entrusted with spirit by the Former Emperor and linked in splendor with Your Majesty—truly he should exhaust the strength of arms and legs and add loyalty atop it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie wept: "A man in plain cloth still dies for one who knows him. I was entrusted by the Former Emperor and shine beside Your Majesty. I should spend my limbs and add loyalty."

sentences.zh: 但臣出入喉膂，每跨時要，及於寵靈輝赫，聞之遐邇。

translations.literal: But your subject goes in and out at the throat and gullet and each time crosses the timely key; reaching the splendor of favor and spiritual grace, it is heard far and near.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet I pass through the throat of power and each time cross the timely post. Favor has grown radiant and is heard far and near."

sentences.zh: 復參宰匠，機政畢歸，震主之聲，見忌必矣。

translations.literal: Again participating as chief craftsman, machine and government entirely return; the sound that shakes the ruler—being envied is certain.
translations.idiomatic: "Again I share the chief craft; machine and government all return to me. The sound that shakes the ruler is sure to be envied."

sentences.zh: 此乃周旦遁逃，成王疑惑，陛下愛臣，便為未盡始終之美。

translations.literal: This is precisely the Duke of Zhou's flight in concealment and King Cheng's doubt; Your Majesty loves your subject and then has not yet completed the beauty of beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: "This is the Duke of Zhou in flight and King Cheng in doubt. Your Majesty loves me yet has not completed the beauty of beginning and end."

sentences.zh: 臣非所以惡華捐勢，非所以辭勤請逸，正希仰成陛下日鏡之明，下念愚臣忘退之禍。

translations.literal: Your subject is not therefore hating glory and casting off power, not therefore declining diligence and requesting ease—he only hopes to look up and complete Your Majesty's mirror-bright day and below to mind this foolish subject's forgetting to withdraw and its calamity.
translations.idiomatic: "I do not hate glory or cast off power, nor decline diligence to seek ease. I only hope to complete Your Majesty's mirror-bright day above and spare me the calamity of forgetting to withdraw below."

sentences.zh: 」高祖久之曰：「吾尋思汝言，理實難奪。

translations.literal: " Gaozu was long silent and said: "I have pondered your words; the principle truly cannot be wrested away.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was silent a long while. "I have pondered your words. The principle cannot be wrested away."

sentences.zh: 」乃手詔世宗曰：「汝第六叔父勰，清規懋賞，與白雲俱潔；

translations.literal: " He then personally wrote an edict to Shizong saying: "Your sixth uncle Xie—pure regulation and splendid reward, with white clouds equally clean;
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote Shizong by his own hand: "Your sixth uncle Xie keeps pure regulation and splendid reward, clean as white clouds;"

sentences.zh: 厭榮捨紱，以松竹為心。

translations.literal: weary of glory and casting off the sash, with pine and bamboo as heart.
translations.idiomatic: "weary of glory and casting off rank, with pine and bamboo for a heart."

sentences.zh: 吾少與綢繆，提攜道趣。

translations.literal: I from youth was intimate with him and led him in the way's intent.
translations.idiomatic: "From youth I was intimate with him and led him in the way."

sentences.zh: 每請解朝纓，恬真丘壑，吾以長兄之重，未忍離遠。

translations.literal: Each time he requested to remove the court sash and dwell in true hills and ravines—I, because of the weight of elder brother, could not bear to part far.
translations.idiomatic: "Each time he asked to leave court and dwell in true hills I, as elder brother, could not bear to let him go far."

sentences.zh: 何容仍屈素業，長嬰世網。

translations.literal: How can he still be bent to plain vocation and long entangled in the age's net?
translations.idiomatic: "How can he still be bent to plain vocation and long entangled in the world's net?"

sentences.zh: 吾百年之後，其聽勰辭蟬捨冕，遂其沖挹之性。

translations.literal: After my hundred years listen to Xie resign the cicada and cast off the crown and follow his pure restraint's nature.
translations.idiomatic: "After my hundred years let Xie resign rank and crown and follow his pure restraint."

sentences.zh: 無使成王之朝，翻疑姬旦之聖，不亦善乎。

translations.literal: Do not let the court of King Cheng turn and doubt the Duke of Zhou's sagehood—is that not good?
translations.idiomatic: "Do not let King Cheng's court turn and doubt the Duke of Zhou's sagehood. Is that not good?"

sentences.zh: 汝為孝子，勿違吾敕。」

translations.literal: You as filial son—do not disobey my command."
translations.idiomatic: "You are a filial son. Do not disobey my command."

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩于行宮，遏祕喪事，獨與右僕射、任城王澄及左右數人為計，奉遷高祖於安車中，勰等出入如平常，視疾進膳，可決外奏。

translations.literal: When Gaozu passed away at the traveling palace they restrained and concealed the mourning; Xie alone with Right Vice Director, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, and a few at left and right made plans, conveying Gaozu into the comfort carriage; Xie and the others went in and out as on ordinary days, viewing illness and advancing food; outside memorials could be decided.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died at the traveling palace they concealed the mourning. Xie alone with Right Vice Director Prince Cheng of Rencheng and a few close attendants laid plans, moved Gaozu into the comfort carriage, and went in and out as on ordinary days, still attending illness and serving food while deciding outside memorials.

sentences.zh: 累日達宛城，乃夜進安車於郡廳事，得加斂櫬，還載臥輿。

translations.literal: After many days they reached Wancheng; then at night they advanced the comfort carriage into the commandery hall, were able to add the inner coffin, and returned carrying the lying carriage.
translations.idiomatic: After many days they reached Wancheng. At night they brought the comfort carriage into the commandery hall, enclosed the coffin, and returned in the lying carriage.

sentences.zh: 六軍內外莫有知者。

translations.literal: Within and without the six armies none knew.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the six armies, no one knew.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人張儒，奉詔徵世宗會駕。

translations.literal: They sent Palace Attendant Zhang Ru with an edict to summon Shizong to join the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: They sent palace attendant Zhang Ru with an edict to summon Shizong to join the carriage.

sentences.zh: 梓宮至魯陽，乃發喪行服。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached Luyang they then issued mourning and put on mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin reached Luyang they issued mourning and put on mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，勰跪授高祖遺敕數紙。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne Xie knelt and handed over several sheets of Gaozu's testamentary command.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne Xie knelt and handed over Gaozu's testamentary sheets.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧疑勰為變，停在魯陽郡外，久之乃入。

translations.literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi suspected Xie of rebellion and halted outside Luyang commandery; after a long time he then entered.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang suspected Xie of rebellion and halted outside Luyang a long time before entering.

sentences.zh: 謂勰曰：「汝非但辛勤，亦危險至極。

translations.literal: He said to Xie: "You are not only toilsome—you are also perilous to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: He told Xie, "You were not only toilsome—you were perilous to the extreme."

sentences.zh: 」勰恨之，對曰：「兄識高年長，故知有夷險，彥和握蛇騎虎，不覺艱難。

translations.literal: " Xie resented it and replied: "Elder brother's understanding is high and years long—therefore you know there is peace and peril; Yanhe grasps a snake and rides a tiger and does not feel hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Xie answered with resentment, "Elder brother's understanding is high and your years are long, so you know peace and peril. Yanhe grasped a snake and rode a tiger and felt no hardship."

sentences.zh: 」禧曰：「汝恨吾後至耳！

translations.literal: " Xi said: "You resent that I arrived late!
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "You resent that I came late!"

sentences.zh: 」自高祖不豫，勰常居中，親侍醫藥，夙夜不離左右，至於衣帶罕解，亂首垢面。

translations.literal: " From when Gaozu was unwell Xie constantly was at the center, personally attending medicine; day and night he did not leave left and right; reaching to garments and belt rarely unfastened, disordered hair and dirty face.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozu's illness Xie constantly attended at the center, personally tending medicine day and night without leaving his side, rarely unfastening belt or garments, hair disordered and face unwashed.

sentences.zh: 帝患久多忿，因之以遷怒。

translations.literal: The emperor's long illness had many angers and thereby shifted anger onto others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's long illness bred many angers, and he turned them on those around him.

sentences.zh: 勰每被誚詈，言至厲切，威責近侍，動將誅斬。

translations.literal: Xie was each time scolded and reviled; words reached severity; authority reproached close attendants and movement was about to behead.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was often scolded in words severe enough to kill; authority fell on attendants and death followed.

sentences.zh: 勰承顏悉心，多所匡濟。

translations.literal: Xie received the expression with full heart and in many cases corrected and aided.
translations.idiomatic: Xie bore the face with full heart and in many cases corrected and aided.

sentences.zh: 及高祖昇遐，陳顯達奔遁始爾，慮凶問洩漏，致有逼迫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended to the far journey Chen Xianda had just begun to flee in defeat; they feared the evil news would leak and there would be pressing force.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu ascended the far journey Chen Xianda had just begun to flee; they feared the evil news would leak and bring pressing force.

sentences.zh: 勰內雖悲慟，外示吉容，出入俯仰，神貌無異。

translations.literal: Within Xie though grieved and moved, without he showed auspicious expression; in going out and coming in, bowing and looking up, divine appearance was without difference.
translations.idiomatic: Within, Xie grieved; without, he showed an auspicious face. In going out and coming in, bowing and looking up, his divine bearing never changed.

sentences.zh: 及至魯陽也，東宮官屬，多疑勰有異志，竊懷防懼。

translations.literal: When they reached Luyang also, the Eastern Palace's official attendants mostly suspected Xie of a different intent and secretly harbored guard and fear.
translations.idiomatic: At Luyang also, the Eastern Palace's officers mostly suspected Xie of different intent and secretly guarded against him.

sentences.zh: 而勰推誠盡禮，卒無纖介。

translations.literal: Yet Xie pushed sincerity to the utmost in ritual and in the end had not the slightest fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xie pushed sincerity to the utmost in ritual and in the end showed not the slightest fault.

sentences.zh: 勰上高祖諡議：「謹案諡法，協時肇享曰『孝』，五宗安之曰『孝』，道德博聞曰『文』，經緯天地曰『文』，仰惟大行皇帝，義實該之，宜上尊號為孝文皇帝，廟曰高祖，陵曰長陵。

translations.literal: Xie submitted Gaozu's posthumous-title deliberation: "Respectfully according to the law of posthumous titles: harmonizing the times and inaugurating enjoyment is called 'Filial'; securing the five kindreds is called 'Filial'; virtue broadly heard is called 'Cultured'; threading heaven and earth is called 'Cultured.' Looking up and considering the late emperor, the meaning truly covers these; the honored title should be Emperor Filial Cultured; temple name Gaozu; tomb name Long Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Xie submitted Gaozu's posthumous-title deliberation: "According to the law of posthumous titles, harmonizing the times and securing the five kindreds is 'Filial'; virtue broadly heard and threading heaven and earth is 'Cultured.' The late emperor's meaning truly covers these. The honored title should be Emperor Filial Cultured; temple name Gaozu; tomb name Long Mound."

sentences.zh: 」世宗從之。

translations.literal: " Shizong followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong approved.

sentences.zh: 既葬，世宗固以勰為宰輔。

translations.literal: After the burial Shizong firmly made Xie chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial Shizong pressed Xie to serve as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 勰頻口陳遺旨，請遂素懷。

translations.literal: Xie repeatedly spoke to his face of the testamentary intent and requested to follow his plain wish.
translations.idiomatic: Xie repeatedly cited the testament and asked to follow his plain wish.

sentences.zh: 世宗對勰悲慟，每不許之。

translations.literal: Shizong toward Xie was grieved and moved and each time did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, grieving toward Xie, each time refused.

sentences.zh: 勰頻煩表聞，辭義懇切。

translations.literal: Xie repeatedly submitted memorials and spoke; the words and meaning were earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Xie repeatedly memorialized in earnest words.

sentences.zh: 世宗難違遺敕，遂其雅情，猶逼以外任，乃以勰為使持節、侍中、都督冀定幽瀛營安平七州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、開府、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Shizong found it hard to go against the testamentary command and followed his elegant wish; still he pressed him with an outside post; therefore he made Xie Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander of Military Affairs in Ji, Ding, You, Ying, and Anping's seven provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Opener of the Office, and Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong could not override the testament yet wished to honor his elegance; still pressing an outside post, he made Xie bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander of military affairs in the seven provinces of Ji, Ding, You, Ying, and Anping, grand general of agile cavalry, opener of the office, and governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 勰仍陳讓，又面申前意，世宗固執不許，乃述職。

translations.literal: Xie still memorialized decline and again spoke to his face the former intent; Shizong firmly held and did not permit; he then took up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Xie still declined and spoke his former intent to his face; Shizong firmly refused; he then took up his post.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王肅等奏：「臣等聞旌功表德，道貴前王；

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Su and others memorialized: "Your subjects have heard that displaying merit and marking virtue—the way esteems former kings;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Su and others memorialized: "We have heard that to display merit and mark virtue is the way of former kings;"

sentences.zh: 庸勳親親，義高盛典。

translations.literal: merit for service, kin for kin—the meaning is lofty in great canon.
translations.idiomatic: "merit for service and kin for kin is lofty in great canon."

sentences.zh: 是故姬旦翼周，光宅曲阜；

translations.literal: Therefore the Duke of Zhou assisted Zhou and brightly dwelt at Qufu;
translations.idiomatic: "Therefore the Duke of Zhou assisted Zhou and brightly dwelt at Qufu;"

sentences.zh: 東平宰漢，寵絕列蕃。

translations.literal: the Eastern Prince governed Han and favor surpassed the array of feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: "the Eastern Prince governed Han and favor surpassed the feudatories."

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰景思內昭，英風外發，協廓乾規，掃氛漢沔。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie—bright thought within, heroic wind without, harmonizing and broadening Qian's regulation, sweeping the vapors of Han and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: "Prince Xie of Pengcheng's bright thought shines within and heroic wind without; he harmonized Qian's regulation and swept the vapors of Han and Mian."

sentences.zh: 屬先帝在天，鳳旌旋斾，靜一六師，肅寧南服。

translations.literal: When the Former Emperor was in Heaven the phoenix banner turned its staffs; he quieted the six armies in one and solemnly pacified the southern submission.
translations.idiomatic: "When the Former Emperor was in Heaven the phoenix banner turned homeward; he quieted the six armies at once and solemnly pacified the south."

sentences.zh: 登聖皇於天衢，開有魏之靈祐，論道中鉉，王猷以穆，七德丕宣，九功在詠。

translations.literal: He set the sage emperor on the heavenly ford and opened the spiritual blessing of Great Wei; deliberating the way at the center pivot, royal plans thereby became solemn; the seven virtues greatly proclaimed, the nine achievements in song.
translations.idiomatic: "He set the sage emperor on the heavenly ford and opened Great Wei's blessing; deliberating the way at the center, royal plans grew solemn; the seven virtues were proclaimed and the nine achievements sung."

sentences.zh: 臣等參詳，宜增邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: Your subjects jointly examined and deem fit to increase fief by one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: "We jointly examined and deem his fief should increase by one thousand five hundred households."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「覽奏，倍增崩絕，未足以上酬勳德，且可如奏。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Having read the memorial, doubled grief at the collapse—still not enough to repay merit and virtue on high; for the time being, as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "Reading the memorial doubles my grief at the collapse—still not enough to repay his merit. For now, as memorialized."

sentences.zh: 」勰頻表固讓，世宗許之。

translations.literal: " Xie repeatedly memorialized firm decline; Shizong permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie repeatedly memorialized firm decline; Shizong permitted it.

sentences.zh: 世宗與勰書曰：「恪奉辭暨今，悲戀哽咽，歲月易遠，便迫暮冬，每思聞道，奉承風教。

translations.literal: Shizong wrote to Xie: "Since parting at the farewell I have been choked with grief; years and months easily far—already pressing toward late winter; each time I think of hearing the way I receive and follow the wind's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong wrote Xie: "Since our farewell grief has choked me. Months slip away and late winter presses. I think constantly of hearing your teaching and following your way."

sentences.zh: 父既辭榮閑外，無容頓違至德。

translations.literal: Father has already resigned glory and rests outside; I cannot for a moment suddenly go against utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: "Father has resigned glory and rests apart; I cannot for a moment go against utmost virtue."

sentences.zh: 出蕃累朔，荒馳實深。

translations.literal: Going out to the feudatory many months—the desolation of parting is truly deep.
translations.idiomatic: "You have been in the feudatory many months—the desolation of parting is deep."

sentences.zh: 今遣主書劉道斌奉宣悲戀，願父來望，必當屆京。

translations.literal: Now I send Chief Clerk Liu Daobin to convey grief and longing; I wish Father to come and look—surely he will reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: "Now I send chief clerk Liu Daobin with my grief and longing. I wish Father to come and look—surely you will reach the capital."

sentences.zh: 展洩哀窮，指不云遠。

translations.literal: To unfold and release sorrow's end—the finger does not say far.
translations.idiomatic: "To unfold sorrow's end—the day is not far."

sentences.zh: 」勰乃朝於京師。

translations.literal: " Xie then attended court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xie then came to court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 景明初，蕭寶卷豫州刺史裴叔業以壽春內屬，詔勰都督南征諸軍事，餘官如故，與尚書令王肅迎接壽春。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Xiao Baojuan's Yuzhou Inspector Pei Shuye with Shouyang submitted to the inner; an edict made Xie Commander of All Armies on the Southern Expedition, other offices as before, and with Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Su to welcome Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingming, Xiao Baojuan's Yuzhou inspector Pei Shuye submitted Shouyang to the inner. Xie was ordered commander of all armies on the southern expedition with other offices unchanged, and with Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Su to welcome Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「五教治樞，古難其選，自非親賢兼切，莫應斯舉。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The five teachings govern the pivot; since antiquity choosing for it has been hard. Unless one is kin, worthy, and urgently needed, none should answer this call."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "The five teachings sit at the heart of rule, and since antiquity the right choice has been rare. Only kin who are also worthy and urgently needed should take up this charge."

sentences.zh: 王以明德懋親，任屬保傅，出居蕃陝，入御袞章，內外克諧，民神攸屬。

translations.literal: The King, with bright virtue and earnest kinship, was entrusted as guardian and tutor; going out he guarded the border marches, coming in he wore the grand regalia—inward and outward in harmony, people and spirits alike attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: The king's bright virtue and close kinship made him guardian and tutor; abroad he held the frontier, at court he wore the grand robes—within and without in harmony, and people and spirits alike looked to him.

sentences.zh: 今董率戎麾，威號宜重，可復授司徒，以光望實。

translations.literal: Now, leading the army's banner, his awesomeness and title should weigh heavy; he may again be granted Minister over the Masses to brighten his repute and substance.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he led the army, his prestige deserved weight; he was again made Minister over the Masses to magnify his standing.

sentences.zh: 」又詔勰以本官領揚州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict also made Xie, in his present office, concurrently Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict kept his present offices and added inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 勰簡刑導禮，與民休息，州境無虞，遐邇安靜。

translations.literal: Xie simplified punishments and guided ritual; he rested the people. Within the province there was no trouble; far and near were quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Xie eased punishments, guided ritual, and let the people rest; the province was untroubled and far and near were calm.

sentences.zh: 揚州所統建安戍主胡景略猶為寶卷拒守不下，勰水陸討之，景略面縛出降。

translations.literal: Within Yang Province's jurisdiction, the Jian'an garrison commander Hu Jinglue still held out for Baojuan and would not submit; Xie attacked by land and water, and Jinglue came out bound in person to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an garrison commander Hu Jinglue still held for Baojuan; Xie attacked by land and water until Jinglue came out bound to surrender.

sentences.zh: 自勰之至壽春，東定城戍，至於陽石，西降建安，山蠻順命，斬首獲生，以數萬計。

translations.literal: From Xie's arrival at Shouchun, he pacified eastern garrisons and towns as far as Yangshi; in the west Jian'an submitted; mountain tribes obeyed; heads taken and captives numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: From Shouchun he secured the east to Yangshi, took Jian'an in the west, won the mountain tribes, and counted tens of thousands in heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 進位大司馬，領司徒，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Marshal and continued as Minister over the Masses; the rest was as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand marshal while keeping the ministry; all else unchanged.

sentences.zh: 增邑八百戶。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief grew by eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又寶卷遣將陳伯之屯於肥口，胡松又據梁城，水軍相繼二百餘里。

translations.literal: Again Baojuan sent the general Chen Bozhi to camp at Feikou, and Hu Song held Liang city; the water army stretched in succession for more than two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Baojuan again sent Chen Bozhi to Feikou and Hu Song to Liang city, with a water line over two hundred li.

sentences.zh: 勰部分將士，分攻諸營，伯之、胡松率眾出戰，諸將擊之，斬首九千，俘獲一萬。

translations.literal: Xie disposed his officers and men to attack the camps separately; Bozhi and Hu Song led their masses out to fight; the generals struck them and took nine thousand heads and ten thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: Xie split his forces against the camps; Bozhi and Hu Song came out and were beaten—nine thousand heads and ten thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 伯之等僅以身免，屯於烽火。

translations.literal: Bozhi and the others barely escaped with their lives and camped at Fenghuo.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi and the rest barely escaped and camped at Fenghuo.

sentences.zh: 勰又分命諸將頻戰，伯之計窮宵遁。

translations.literal: Xie again ordered the generals to fight repeatedly; Bozhi's plans were exhausted and he fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Xie ordered repeated attacks until Bozhi's plans failed and he fled by night.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，詔曰：「王戚尊上輔，德勳莫二，孤心昧識，訓保攸憑。

translations.literal: The Huainan region was pacified. An edict said: "The King, as kin, honors the highest minister; in merit and virtue he has no second. My heart is dim in knowledge; in instruction and guardianship I rely on him."
translations.idiomatic: Huainan was pacified. An edict said: "As kin you honor the highest minister; in merit none stands beside you. My judgment is dim—I lean on you for counsel and guard."

sentences.zh: 比以壽春初開，鎮壓任重，故令王親董元戎，遠撫淮外。

translations.literal: Lately, when Shouchun was first opened, the duty of suppression was weighty; therefore the King was ordered personally to direct the main army and pacify the far Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouchun first fell the burden of holding it was heavy, so you were sent in person to command the host and pacify the Huai frontier.

sentences.zh: 冒茲炎蒸，衡蓋飄颻，經略踰時，必有虧損。

translations.literal: Braving this scorching heat, with canopy and carriage swaying in the wind, prolonged campaigning over time must bring loss and harm.
translations.idiomatic: You braved this heat with canopy and carriage in the wind; long campaigning must wear you down.

sentences.zh: 淹違詣覿，夙夜係情。

translations.literal: Long kept from audience, day and night my feelings are bound to you.
translations.idiomatic: Kept from audience so long, day and night my heart is bound to you.

sentences.zh: 兼制勝宣規，威效兼著，公私允稱，義所欽嘉。

translations.literal: Moreover your victories and plans were proclaimed together, awe and effect both manifest; public and private alike approved—righteousness demands admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Your victories and plans together showed their power; public and private alike praised what duty required us to honor.

sentences.zh: 雖凱旋有期，無申延屬，可遣給事黃門侍郎鄭道昭就彼祗勞。

translations.literal: Though triumph has a set day, I cannot defer my longing; Palace Attendant of the Yellow Gate Zheng Daozhao may go there to pay respects on my behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Though your return is fixed, I cannot wait to see you—send Palace Attendant Zheng Daozhao to greet you there."

sentences.zh: 」徵勰還朝。

translations.literal: Xie was summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 勰政崇寬裕，絲毫不犯，淮南士庶，追其餘惠，至今思之。

translations.literal: Xie's government honored leniency; he did not violate the slightest thing. The gentry and commoners of Huainan pursued his remaining kindness and still think of him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie ruled with leniency and touched nothing unjust; Huainan's people still cherish what he left them.

sentences.zh: 初，勰之定壽春也，獲蕭寶卷汝陰太守王果、豫州治中庾禝等數人，勰傾衿禮之，常參坐席。

translations.literal: At first, when Xie pacified Shouchun, he captured Xiao Baojuan's Administrator of Ruyin Wang Guo, Yu Province aide Yu Ji, and several others; Xie opened his breast in courtesy to them and often had them share his seat.
translations.idiomatic: When he took Shouchun he captured Baojuan's Ruyin administrator Wang Guo, Yu Province aide Yu Ji, and others; Xie treated them with open courtesy and often seated them beside him.

sentences.zh: 果承間進曰：「果等契闊生平，皓首播越，顧瞻西夕，餘光幾何。

translations.literal: Guo seized an interval to advance and said: "Guo and the others have been torn from their lives' bond; white hair is scattered abroad; looking west at the setting sun, how little light remains."
translations.idiomatic: Guo spoke up: "We have been torn from our life's bond; white hair is scattered abroad; looking west at the setting sun, how little light remains."

sentences.zh: 今遭聖化，正應力茲愚老，申展尺寸，但在南百口，生死分張，乞還江外，以申德澤。

translations.literal: "Now we meet sage transformation and ought to exert what strength these foolish old men have and show our measure—but south of the river we have a hundred mouths, life and death divided; we beg to return beyond the river and declare your virtuous grace."
translations.idiomatic: "Now under your sage rule we should exert what these old men still have—but south of the river a hundred mouths stand divided between life and death; let us return beyond the river and declare your grace."

sentences.zh: 」勰矜而許之。

translations.literal: Xie pitied them and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie pitied them and agreed.

sentences.zh: 果又謝曰：「殿下賜處，有過國士。

translations.literal: Guo thanked him again, saying: "Your Highness's treatment of us has surpassed a state's scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Guo thanked him again: "Your Highness has treated us beyond what a state's scholar deserves."

sentences.zh: 果等今還，仰負慈澤，請聽仁駕振旅，反跡江外。

translations.literal: "Guo and the others now return, bearing your kind grace on our backs; we ask leave for your benevolent carriage to shake the army and turn our tracks beyond the river."
translations.idiomatic: "We go home carrying your kindness on our backs; grant your carriage to shake the host so we may turn our steps beyond the river."

sentences.zh: 」至此乃還。

translations.literal: Only then did they return.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did they return.

sentences.zh: 其為遠人所懷如此。

translations.literal: Such was how the distant held him in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: So deeply did distant peoples hold him in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 勰至京師，世宗臨東堂引見，詔勰曰：「比鳳皇未至，[2]蒼黎二化，故仰屈尊謨，綏懷邊附，而寇豎昏迷，敢鬬淮楚。

translations.literal: When Xie reached the capital, Shizong received him at the Eastern Hall and addressed Xie: "Lately the phoenix has not come,[2] the dark masses are in two transformations—therefore I bent your honored counsel to soothe and cherish the border adherents; yet the bandit chieftain was benighted and dared fight in Huai-Chu."
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Shizong received him in the Eastern Hall and said: "The phoenix has not yet come,[2] the people stand between two orders—so I bent your counsel to win the frontier; yet that benighted bandit dared fight in Huai-Chu."

sentences.zh: 叔父英略高明，應機殄定，凱旋今辰，伏慰悲佇。

translations.literal: "Uncle's heroic strategy is lofty and bright; responding to the moment you extinguished and settled them; triumph this day—prostrate, I ease my sorrowful waiting."
translations.idiomatic: "Uncle, your strategy is bright; you answered the moment and ended them. Today's triumph eases what I have long grieved and waited for."

sentences.zh: 」勰謝曰：「臣忝充戍帥，撫安新故，而不能宣武導恩，威懷遐邇。

translations.literal: Xie thanked him, saying: "Your servant disgracefully fills the post of frontier commander, pacifying the new and the old, yet could not spread martial power and guide grace, aweing and cherishing far and near."
translations.idiomatic: Xie replied: "I disgracefully held the frontier and could not spread force and grace to awe far and near."

sentences.zh: 致小豎伯之，驅率蟻徒，侵擾邊堡。

translations.literal: "This caused the petty chieftain Bozhi to drive ant-like followers and harass the border forts."
translations.idiomatic: "That let the petty Bozhi drive ant-like followers against our border forts."

sentences.zh: 非唯仰慚天顏，實亦俯愧朝列。

translations.literal: "Not only do I look up ashamed before Heaven's face; in truth I also bow my head ashamed before the court ranks."
translations.idiomatic: "I am ashamed before your face and before the court alike."

sentences.zh: 春秋責帥，臣實當之。

translations.literal: "The Spring and Autumn Annals blame the commander; your servant truly bears it."
translations.idiomatic: "Spring and Autumn blames the commander—and that blame is mine."

sentences.zh: 賴陛下慈深捨過，故使愚臣獲免罪責。

translations.literal: "Relying on Your Majesty's deep mercy in setting aside faults, therefore this foolish servant escaped punishment."
translations.idiomatic: "Only your deep mercy let this fool escape punishment."

sentences.zh: 」勰頻表辭大司馬、領司徒及所增邑，乞還中山。

translations.literal: Xie repeatedly memorialized to resign Grand Marshal, concurrent Minister over the Masses, and the added fief, begging to return to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie repeatedly asked to resign grand marshal, the ministry, and the added fief and return to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 有詔不許。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused.

sentences.zh: 乃除錄尚書、侍中，司徒如故。

translations.literal: He was then made Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant; Minister over the Masses as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made recorder of the Masters of Writing and palace attendant while keeping the ministry.

sentences.zh: 固辭不免。

translations.literal: He firmly refused but could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: He refused firmly but could not escape office.

sentences.zh: 勰雅好恬素，不以勢利嬰心。

translations.literal: Xie by nature loved quiet simplicity and did not let power and profit touch his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xie loved quiet simplicity and let power and profit never touch his heart.

sentences.zh: 高祖重其事幹，縶維不許。

translations.literal: Gaozu valued his capacity for affairs and would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu valued his capacity and would not release him.

sentences.zh: 雖臨崩遺詔，復世宗留連，每乖情願。

translations.literal: Though at the verge of death the testament again had Shizong detain him; each time it went against his wish.
translations.idiomatic: Even the deathbed testament had Shizong keep him—each time against his wish.

sentences.zh: 常悽然歎息，以詔旨殷勤，僶俛應命。

translations.literal: He often sighed in sorrow; because the edict's words were earnest, he bent his will and answered the charge.
translations.idiomatic: He often sighed; when the edict pressed earnestly he bent his will and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 時咸陽王禧漸以驕矜，頗有不法，北海王詳陰言於世宗，世宗深忌之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Xi of Xianyang grew daily proud and had many unlawful acts; Prince Xiang of Beihai spoke of it privately to Shizong, and Shizong deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang grew proud and lawless; Prince Xiang of Beihai spoke privately to Shizong, who came to resent him deeply.

sentences.zh: 又言勰大得人情，不宜久在宰輔，勸世宗遵高祖遺敕。

translations.literal: He also said Xie had won great popular feeling and ought not long remain chief minister, urging Shizong to follow Gaozu's testament charge.
translations.idiomatic: He also said Xie had won the people's hearts and should not long stay chief minister, urging Shizong to follow Gaozu's testament.

sentences.zh: 禧等又出領軍于烈為恒州，非烈情願，固強之，烈深以為忿。

translations.literal: Xi and the others also sent out the commander of the army Yu Lie as Hengzhou inspector—not Lie's wish; they forced him firmly, and Lie deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and the others also sent army commander Yu Lie to Hengzhou—not his wish; they forced him, and he burned with resentment.

sentences.zh: 烈子忠嘗在左右，密令忠言於世宗云：「諸王等意不可測，宜廢之，早自覽政。

translations.literal: Lie's son Zhong had once been at the emperor's side; he secretly ordered Zhong to tell Shizong: "The princes' intentions cannot be measured; they should be removed and Your Majesty should early take government into his own view."
translations.idiomatic: Lie's son Zhong, once at court, was told in secret: "The princes' minds cannot be read—remove them and take the reins early."

sentences.zh: 」時將礿祭，王公並齋於廟東坊。

translations.literal: At that time the autumn di sacrifice was due; the princes and dukes all fasted in the temple's eastern lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn di sacrifice was due; princes and dukes fasted in the temple's eastern lodge.

sentences.zh: 世宗遣于烈將宿衞壯士六十餘人召禧、勰、詳等，引入，見之於光極殿。

translations.literal: Shizong sent Yu Lie with more than sixty stalwart night guards to summon Xi, Xie, Xiang, and the others, bring them in, and receive them at the Hall of Ultimate Light.
