translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent Yu Lie with sixty-odd night guards to summon Xi, Xie, Xiang, and the rest to the Hall of Ultimate Light.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂勰曰：「頃來南北務殷，不容仰遂沖操。

translations.literal: Shizong said to Xie: "Lately north-south affairs have been pressing; I could not honor your lofty withdrawal."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong told Xie: "North and south have pressed me—I could not honor your wish to withdraw."

sentences.zh: 恪是何人，而敢久違先敕，今遂叔父高蹈之意。

translations.literal: "What sort of man is Ke that he dares long defy the former charge? Now I follow uncle's intent to tread the high path."
translations.idiomatic: "What is Ke that he should defy the former charge? Now I grant uncle's wish to walk the high path."

sentences.zh: 」勰謝曰：「先帝不以臣虛薄，曲垂罔己之澤，出入綢繆，公私無捨。

translations.literal: Xie thanked him, saying: "The late emperor, not deeming your servant shallow and slight, bent down the grace of not forgetting me; in and out we were bound close, public and private without reserve."
translations.idiomatic: Xie replied: "The late emperor, not deeming me slight, bent down grace that never forgot me; in and out we were bound, public and private without reserve."

sentences.zh: 自陛下龍飛九五，屢求解落，既為宰輔所抑，亦不為陛下所許。

translations.literal: "Since Your Majesty's dragon flew to the ninety-fifth degree, I have repeatedly sought release; the chief ministers suppressed it, and Your Majesty also would not grant it."
translations.idiomatic: "Since Your Majesty took the throne I have sought release again and again—the ministers blocked it and you would not grant it."

sentences.zh: 先歲夏中，重塵天聽，時蒙優借，出為定州。

translations.literal: "In midsummer of the year before last I again dusted Heaven's hearing; then I was graciously lent out as Dingzhou inspector."
translations.idiomatic: "Midsummer before last I troubled Heaven's ear again and was lent out as Dingzhou inspector."

sentences.zh: 往年還洛陽，敕總戎淮肥，雖無功效，幸免罪戾。

translations.literal: "The year before I returned to Luoyang and was ordered to command the Huai-Fei armies; though without merit I barely escaped guilt."
translations.idiomatic: "The year before I returned to Luoyang and was ordered to command Huai-Fei; though I achieved little I barely escaped blame."

sentences.zh: 云歸未幾，復委臣以非據之任。

translations.literal: "Hardly had I returned when I was again entrusted with a post beyond my measure."
translations.idiomatic: "Hardly home, I was again given a post beyond my measure."

sentences.zh: 臣頻煩干請，具簡聖聽。

translations.literal: "Your servant has repeatedly troubled requests, all set out plainly to the sage ear."
translations.idiomatic: "I have troubled you with requests, all plainly set before your ear."

sentences.zh: 陛下孝深無改，仰遵先詔，上成睿明之美，下遂微臣之志，感惟今往，悲喜交深。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty's filial depth is without change; looking up you follow the former edict, above completing the beauty of sagely clarity, below fulfilling this petty servant's wish—moved by present and past, joy and sorrow interweave."
translations.idiomatic: "Your filial heart is unchanged; you follow the former edict above, complete sagely clarity, and below fulfill my wish—past and present move me, joy and sorrow together."

sentences.zh: 」乃詔曰：「王宿尚閑靜，志捐世務，先帝愛亮之至，弗奪此情，遺敕炳然，許遂沖退。

translations.literal: An edict then said: "The King from old has honored quiet; his will abandons worldly affairs. The late emperor loved and brightened this to the utmost and would not seize that feeling; the testament is clear and permits this lofty withdrawal."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The king has long honored quiet and abandoned worldly affairs. The late emperor loved that brightness and would not seize it; the testament clearly permits this withdrawal."

sentences.zh: 雅操不移，朕亦未敢違奪。

translations.literal: "His refined conduct does not shift; I too have not dared to violate and seize it."
translations.idiomatic: "His refined conduct does not shift; I too have not dared to seize it."

sentences.zh: 今乃釋位歸第，丘園是營，高尚之節，確爾貞固，賁、履之操，邈焉難追。

translations.literal: "Now he releases office and returns to his residence; hill and garden are his to tend—lofty conduct, firm and true; the integrity of Ben and Lü, far to pursue."
translations.idiomatic: "Now he leaves office for his residence and tends hill and garden—conduct lofty and firm, the integrity of Ben and Lü, hard to follow."

sentences.zh: 而王宅初構，財力多闕，成立之期，歲月莫就。

translations.literal: "Yet the king's house is newly built and funds and strength are much lacking; the term of completion, by months, is not reached."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet his house is newly built and funds are short; completion is still months away."

sentences.zh: 可量遣工役，分給材瓦，禀王所好，速令制辦，務從簡素，以稱王心。

translations.literal: "Measure and send laborers, distribute timber and tile according to the king's liking, quickly have it made—strive for simplicity to match the king's heart."
translations.idiomatic: "Send measured labor and timber and tile as he wishes, build quickly and simply to match his heart."

sentences.zh: 」勰因是作蠅賦以諭懷，惡讒構也。

translations.literal: Xie thereupon composed the "Fly" rhapsody to express his feelings, hating slander and framing.
translations.idiomatic: Xie then wrote the "Fly" rhapsody to voice his feelings, hating slander and plots.

sentences.zh: 又以勰為太師，勰遂固辭。

translations.literal: Again Xie was made Grand Preceptor; Xie then firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made grand preceptor; Xie refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「蓋二儀分象，君臣之位形焉；

translations.literal: An edict said: "The two principles divide their images; the positions of ruler and minister take form."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Heaven and earth divide their signs and ruler and minister take their places."

sentences.zh: 上下既位，唱和之義生焉。

translations.literal: Once upper and lower have their places, the meaning of leading and following arises.
translations.idiomatic: Once ranks are set, leading and following arise.

sentences.zh: 自古統天位主，曷常不賴明師，仗賢輔，而後燮和陰陽，彝倫民物者哉？

translations.literal: Since antiquity, lords who hold Heaven's position—how have they not relied on bright teachers and leaned on worthy assistants, and only afterward harmonized yin and yang and ordered the people's constant norms?
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, who has held Heaven's seat without bright teachers and worthy assistants before harmonizing yin and yang and ordering the people's norms?

sentences.zh: 往而不返者，先民誠有之，斯所謂獨善其身而亂大倫，山林之士耳。

translations.literal: Those who go and do not return—the ancients truly had them; this is what is called keeping goodness for oneself alone while disordering the great norms, the men of mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: Those who go and never return—the ancients knew them too; they kept goodness alone and broke the great norms, men of mountain and forest.

sentences.zh: 賢人君子則不然也。

translations.literal: Worthy men and noble sons are not so.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men and noble sons are not like that.

sentences.zh: 屈己以安民，艱身以濟物，所謂以先知覺後知，同塵而與天下俱潔者也。

translations.literal: They bend themselves to settle the people, strain their persons to aid things—what is called using prior knowledge to awaken later knowledge, sharing dust and cleansing the world together.
translations.idiomatic: They bend themselves to settle the people and strain their persons to aid the world—awakening the late with the early, sharing dust until all are clean.

sentences.zh: 朕猥以沖年，纂臨寶曆，實賴叔父匡濟之功，誠宜永兼將相，以綱維內外。

translations.literal: "I, coarse in tender years, have inherited the precious succession and truly rely on uncle's power to rescue; it is right that he forever hold both general and minister to weave inner and outer."
translations.idiomatic: "Young and coarse on the throne, I truly rely on uncle's rescue; he should forever hold general and minister to weave within and without."

sentences.zh: 但逼奪先旨，憚違沖挹，俛志割心，以遂高素。

translations.literal: "Yet forced to seize the former charge, I fear violating lofty withdrawal; I bend my will and cut my heart to follow high simplicity."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet forced to seize the former charge I feared violating his withdrawal; I bent my will and cut my heart to follow his simplicity."

sentences.zh: 自比水旱乖和，陰陽失序，是以屈王論道，庶燮茲玉燭。

translations.literal: "Lately because flood and drought are out of harmony and yin and yang lose order, I therefore bend the king to discuss the Way, hoping to harmonize this jade candle."
translations.idiomatic: "Lately flood and drought and yin and yang have fallen out of step—so I bend the king to discuss the Way and harmonize the jade candle of rule."

sentences.zh: 且師宰從容，無廢清尚，故周旦復辟而居之，尚父期頤以終位。

translations.literal: "Moreover the teacher-minister may be at ease without abandoning pure elevation—thus the Duke of Zhou returned the government and dwelt in it; the Martial Father ended his post at a full century."
translations.idiomatic: "A teacher-minister may be at ease without losing pure elevation—the Duke of Zhou returned rule yet remained; the Martial Father ended at a full age."

sentences.zh: 王義兼家國，理絕獨高，可遣侍中敦諭。

translations.literal: "The king's righteousness embraces family and state; principle forbids standing alone on high—a palace attendant may go to instruct him earnestly."
translations.idiomatic: "The king's duty embraces family and state; principle forbids standing alone on high—send a palace attendant to instruct him earnestly."

sentences.zh: 」世宗又修家人書於勰曰：「恪言：奉還告承，猶執沖遜，恪實闇寡，政術多粃，匡弼之寄，仰屬親尊。

translations.literal: Shizong also wrote a family letter to Xie: "Ke says: receiving your returned report, you still hold lofty modesty. Ke is truly dim and few; in government craft there is much chaff; the trust of support and correction relies on honored kin."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong also wrote him as family: "Ke says: your report still holds lofty modesty. Ke is dim and few; government has much chaff; support and correction rely on you."

sentences.zh: 父德望兼重，師訓所歸，豈得近遺家國，遠崇清尚也。

translations.literal: "Father's virtue and repute are both weighty; teacherly instruction is where we return—how can we near abandon family and state and far honor pure elevation?"
translations.idiomatic: "Father's virtue and repute are weighty; teacherly instruction is our return—how can we nearly abandon family and state for distant purity?"

sentences.zh: 便願紆降，時副傾注之心。

translations.literal: "I only wish you would bend down in time to match the heart that leans on you."
translations.idiomatic: "Only bend down in time to match the heart that leans on you."

sentences.zh: 」勰不得已而應命。

translations.literal: Xie had no way out and answered the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Xie had no way out and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 世宗後頻幸勰第。

translations.literal: Afterward Shizong repeatedly visited Xie's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Shizong often visited his house.

sentences.zh: 及京兆、廣平暴虐不法，詔宿衞隊主率羽林虎賁，幽守諸王於其第。

translations.literal: When the Jingzhao and Guangping princes were violent and unlawful, an edict ordered the night-guard squad chief to lead feathered forest tiger guards and confine the princes at their residences.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingzhao and Guangping princes turned violent, an edict had the night-guard chief lead tiger guards to confine the princes in their houses.

sentences.zh: 勰上表切諫，世宗不納。

translations.literal: Xie submitted a memorial urgently remonstrating; Shizong did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie memorialized urgently; Shizong would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 勰既無山水之適，又絕知己之遊，唯對妻子，鬱鬱不樂。

translations.literal: Xie, having neither the pleasure of mountains and waters nor the company of knowing friends, faced only wife and children and was depressed and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Without mountains, waters, or knowing friends, he faced only wife and children and grew depressed.

sentences.zh: 議定律令，勰與高陽王雍、八座、朝士有才學者五日一集，參論軌制應否之宜。

translations.literal: When deliberating on statutes and ordinances, Xie together with Prince Yong of Gaoyang, the Eight Seats, and court scholars of talent met every five days to discuss whether the rules and measures were fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When statutes were debated, Xie met every five days with Prince Yong of Gaoyang, the Eight Seats, and learned courtiers to weigh what fit.

sentences.zh: 而勰夙侍高祖，兼聰達博聞，凡所裁決，時彥歸仰。

translations.literal: Moreover Xie from old attended Gaozu and was moreover penetrating and broad in hearing; in whatever he decided, the men of the age looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: He had long attended Gaozu and was penetrating and broad in hearing; whatever he decided, men of the age looked up.

sentences.zh: 加以美容貌，善風儀，端嚴若神，折旋合度，出入言笑，觀者忘疲。

translations.literal: Added to this were fine looks and good bearing; stern as a spirit, turning and advancing in proper measure; in going out, speech, and laughter, viewers forgot fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: Fine looks and bearing, stern as a spirit, every turn measured—in speech and laughter watchers forgot fatigue.

sentences.zh: 又加侍中。

translations.literal: He was again made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 勰敦尚文史，物務之暇，披覽不輟。

translations.literal: Xie honored literature and history; in the intervals of affairs he unceasingly read.
translations.idiomatic: Xie honored literature and history and read without cease between affairs.

sentences.zh: 撰自古帝王賢達至於魏世子孫，三十卷，名曰要略。

translations.literal: He compiled from ancient emperors, kings, and worthies down to Wei imperial sons and grandsons, thirty scrolls, titled Essentials in Brief.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled thirty scrolls from ancient rulers and worthies down to Wei imperial kin, titled Essentials in Brief.

sentences.zh: 小心謹慎，初無過失，雖閑居宴處，亦無慢色惰容。

translations.literal: Careful and cautious, at first he had no faults; even in leisure and feasting he had no slack color or lazy bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Careful from the first, he had no faults; even at leisure he showed no slackness.

sentences.zh: 愛敬儒彥，傾心禮待。

translations.literal: He loved and respected Confucian talents and bent his heart to courtesy toward them.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Confucian talent and bent his heart to courtesy.

sentences.zh: 清正儉素，門無私謁。

translations.literal: Upright, pure, and frugal; his gate had no private callers.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, pure, and frugal—his gate knew no private callers.

sentences.zh: 性仁孝，言於朝廷，以其舅潘僧固為冀州樂陵太守。

translations.literal: By nature he was benevolent and filial; speaking at court, he had his maternal uncle Pan Senggu made Administrator of Leling in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolent and filial by nature, he spoke at court and had his uncle Pan Senggu made Leling administrator in Ji.

sentences.zh: [3]京兆王愉搆逆，僧固見逼從之。

translations.literal: [3] Prince Yu of Jingzhao framed rebellion; Senggu was compelled to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Prince Yu of Jingzhao rebelled; Senggu was forced to follow.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高肇性既凶愎，賊害賢俊。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Gao Zhao by nature was fierce and obstinate and harmed worthy and outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Gao Zhao was fierce by nature and harmed the worthy.

sentences.zh: 又肇之兄女，入為夫人，順皇后崩，世宗欲以為后，勰固執以為不可。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhao's elder brother's daughter entered as consort; when Empress Shun died, Shizong wished to make her empress; Xie firmly held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's brother's daughter had entered the inner quarters; when Empress Shun died Shizong wished to make her empress, and Xie firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 肇於是屢譖勰於世宗，世宗不納。

translations.literal: Zhao therefore repeatedly slandered Xie to Shizong; Shizong did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then slandered Xie again and again; Shizong would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 因僧固之同愉逆，肇誣勰北與愉通，南招蠻賊。

translations.literal: Because Senggu had shared Yu's rebellion, Zhao slandered that Xie in the north communicated with Yu and in the south recruited barbarian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Senggu shared Yu's rebellion, Zhao claimed Xie had conspired with Yu in the north and recruited southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 勰國郎中令魏偃、前防閤高祖珍希肇提攜，搆成其事。

translations.literal: Xie's household chief of the gentlemen Wei Yan and former gate guard Gaozu Zhen hoped for Zhao's promotion and framed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's household chief Wei Yan and former gate guard Gaozu Zhen, hoping for Zhao's favor, framed the affair.

sentences.zh: 肇初令侍中元暉以奏世宗，暉不從，令左衞元珍言之。

translations.literal: At first Zhao ordered Palace Attendant Yuan Hui to memorialize Shizong; Hui would not follow; he ordered Left Guard Yuan Zhen to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao first had Palace Attendant Yuan Hui report to Shizong; Hui refused; he had Left Guard Yuan Zhen speak instead.

sentences.zh: 世宗訪之於暉，暉明勰無此。

translations.literal: Shizong inquired of Hui; Hui made clear Xie had no such thing.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong asked Hui, who made clear Xie had done no such thing.

sentences.zh: 世宗更以問肇，肇以魏偃、祖珍為證，世宗乃信之。

translations.literal: Shizong again asked Zhao; Zhao used Wei Yan and Zhen as proof; Shizong then believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong asked Zhao again; Zhao cited Wei Yan and Zhen as proof, and Shizong believed.

sentences.zh: 永平元年九月，召勰及高陽王雍、廣陽王嘉、清河王懌、廣平王懷及高肇等入。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Yongping, Xie and Prince Yong of Gaoyang, Prince Jia of Guangyang, Prince Yi of Qinghe, Prince Huai of Guangping, and Gao Zhao and others were summoned in.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping year 1, ninth month, Xie and Princes Yong of Gaoyang, Jia of Guangyang, Yi of Qinghe, Huai of Guangping, and Gao Zhao were summoned.

sentences.zh: 時勰妃方產，勰乃固辭不赴。

translations.literal: At that time Xie's consort was in childbirth; Xie therefore firmly refused and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was in childbirth; he firmly refused to go.

sentences.zh: 中使相繼，不得已乃令命駕，意甚憂懼，與妃訣而登車。

translations.literal: Palace envoys came in succession; having no way out he ordered the carriage; his mind was very fearful and anxious; he took leave of his consort and mounted the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys came one after another; he had no choice but to order the carriage, fearful and anxious, and took leave of his consort before mounting.

sentences.zh: 入東掖門，度一小橋，牛不肯進，遂擊之，良久。

translations.literal: Entering the Eastern Flank Gate, crossing a small bridge, the ox would not advance; they struck it a long while.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Flank Gate his ox would not cross a small bridge though they beat it long.

sentences.zh: 更有使者責勰來遲，乃令去牛，人挽而進，宴於禁中。

translations.literal: Again an envoy blamed Xie for coming late; he was ordered to remove the ox; men pulled the carriage forward; they feasted in the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Another envoy blamed his lateness; the ox was removed and men pulled him in; they feasted within the palace.

sentences.zh: 至夜皆醉，各就別所消息。

translations.literal: By night all were drunk; each went to a separate lodging to rest.
translations.idiomatic: By night all were drunk and each went to a separate room to rest.

sentences.zh: 俄而元珍將武士齎毒酒而至。

translations.literal: Soon Yuan Zhen led warriors bearing poisoned wine and arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan Zhen came with warriors bearing poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 勰曰：「吾忠於朝廷，何罪見殺！

translations.literal: Xie said: "I am loyal to the court—what crime brings killing!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie said: "I am loyal to the court—what crime brings death?"

sentences.zh: 一見至尊，死無恨也。

translations.literal: "If I may once see the Supreme One, I die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: "Let me see the emperor once and I die without regret."

sentences.zh: 」珍曰：「至尊何可復見！

translations.literal: Zhen said: "The Supreme One—how can he be seen again!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said: "The emperor—how can you see him again?"

sentences.zh: 王但飲酒。

translations.literal: "The King need only drink the wine."
translations.idiomatic: "Only drink."

sentences.zh: 」勰曰：「至尊聖明，不應無事殺我，求與告我罪者一對曲直。

translations.literal: Xie said: "The Supreme One is sage and bright; he ought not kill me without cause—I beg to face once the one who reports my crime and settle right and wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Xie said: "The emperor is sage and bright; he should not kill me without cause—let me face my accuser once and settle right and wrong."

sentences.zh: 」武士以刀鐶築勰二下。

translations.literal: The warriors struck Xie twice with the ring of the blade.
translations.idiomatic: The warriors struck him twice with the ring of the blade.

sentences.zh: 勰大言曰：「皇天！

translations.literal: Xie cried aloud: "Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie cried: "Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 忠而見殺。

translations.literal: Loyal yet killed.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal—and killed.

sentences.zh: 」武士又以刀鐶築勰。

translations.literal: The warriors again struck Xie with the ring of the blade.
translations.idiomatic: They struck him again with the ring.

sentences.zh: 勰乃飲毒酒，武士就殺之。

translations.literal: Xie then drank the poisoned wine; the warriors thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He drank the poison; the warriors then killed him.

sentences.zh: 向晨，以褥裹屍，輿從屏門而出，載屍歸第，云王因飲而薨。

translations.literal: Toward dawn they wrapped the corpse in a quilt, carried it out through the screen gate, loaded the corpse back to his residence, saying the king had died from drink.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they wrapped the corpse, carried it out the screen gate, and sent it home saying the king had died from drink.

sentences.zh: 勰妃李氏，司空沖之女也，號哭大言曰：「高肇枉理殺人，天道有靈，汝還當惡死。

translations.literal: Xie's consort Lady Li, daughter of Minister of Works Chong, wailed aloud: "Gao Zhao killed a man against reason; Heaven has spirit—you will yet die an evil death."
translations.idiomatic: Consort Lady Li, daughter of Minister Chong, wailed: "Gao Zhao killed against reason; Heaven has spirit—you will yet die wickedly."

sentences.zh: 」及肇以罪見殺，論者知有報應焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao was killed for his crime, discussers knew there was retribution.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was killed for his crimes, men said retribution had come.

sentences.zh: 世宗為舉哀於東堂，給東園第一祕器、朝服一襲、賻錢八十萬、布二千匹、蠟五百斤，大鴻臚護喪事。

translations.literal: Shizong held mourning for him at the Eastern Hall, gave Eastern Garden first-grade secret vessels, one suit of court dress, eighty myriad in condolence money, two thousand bolts of cloth, five hundred jin of wax; the Grand Herald oversaw the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong mourned him in the Eastern Hall and gave Eastern Garden rites, court dress, eighty myriad cash, two thousand bolts of cloth, five hundred jin of wax; the Grand Herald oversaw the funeral.

sentences.zh: 勰既有大功於國，無罪見害，百姓冤之。

translations.literal: Xie had great merit for the state yet was killed without crime; the common people resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie had served the state greatly yet was killed without crime; the people resented it.

sentences.zh: 行路士女，流涕而言曰：「高令公枉殺如此賢王！

translations.literal: Travelers, men and women, wept as they spoke: "Chief Minister Gao wrongly killed so worthy a king!"
translations.idiomatic: Men and women on the road wept and said: "Chief Minister Gao wrongly killed so worthy a king!"

sentences.zh: 」在朝貴賤，莫不喪氣。

translations.literal: At court, noble and base alike, none did not lose spirit.
translations.idiomatic: At court, high and low alike lost heart.

sentences.zh: 追崇假黃鉞、使持節、都督中外諸軍事，司徒公、侍中、太師、王如故。

translations.literal: Posthumous honors: Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, Duke Minister over the Masses, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Prince as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given acting yellow battle-ax, bearer of the staff, commander of all armies, duke minister over the masses, palace attendant, and grand preceptor, prince as before.

sentences.zh: 給鑾輅九旒、虎賁班劍百人、前後部羽葆鼓吹、轀輬車。

translations.literal: Given imperial carriage with nine tassels, a hundred tiger guards with swords of state, front and rear feathered canopy and drum escort, and covered funeral carriage.
translations.idiomatic: They gave him the imperial carriage with nine tassels, a hundred tiger guards with swords of state, front and rear feathered escort, and covered funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 有司奏太常卿劉芳議勰諡曰：「王挺德弱齡，誕資至孝，睿性過人，學不師授。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized that Minister of Rites Liu Fang discussed Xie's posthumous name, saying: "The King from youth raised virtue; he was born with utmost filiality; keen nature surpassed others; learning needed no teacher."
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office reported Minister Liu Fang's posthumous proposal: "The king from youth raised virtue, born to utmost filiality, keen beyond others, learning without teachers."

sentences.zh: 卓爾之操，發自天然；

translations.literal: Outstanding conduct sprang from the natural;
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding conduct sprang from nature;

sentences.zh: 不羣之美，幼而獨出。

translations.literal: uncommon beauty, in youth alone emerging.
translations.idiomatic: uncommon beauty emerged alone in youth.

sentences.zh: 及入參政務，綸綍有光；

translations.literal: When he entered to share government, the imperial commands had luster;
translations.idiomatic: Entering government, his commands shone;

sentences.zh: 爰登中鉉，敷明五教。

translations.literal: ascending the central axis, he spread and clarified the five teachings.
translations.idiomatic: on the central axis he spread the five teachings.

sentences.zh: 漢北告危，皇赫問罪，王內親藥膳，外總六師。

translations.literal: North of Han reported danger; the emperor sternly inquired into guilt; the King inwardly attended the medicine and broth, outwardly commanded the six armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the north of Han cried danger the emperor asked guilt; inwardly he tended the broth, outwardly he commanded the six armies.

sentences.zh: 及宮車晏駕，上下哀慘。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage peacefully halted, above and below were mournful and wretched.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage halted, court and realm mourned.

sentences.zh: 奮猛銜戚，英略潛通，翼衞靈輿，整戎振斾。

translations.literal: Fierce and bold he bore grief; heroic strategy flowed in secret; he winged and guarded the spirit carriage, arrayed the troops and shook the banners.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce in grief, strategy flowing in secret, he guarded the spirit carriage and arrayed troops and banners.

sentences.zh: 歷次宛謝，迄于魯陽，送往奉居，無慚周霍，禀遺作輔，遠至邇安。

translations.literal: Stopping again and again from Wan to Luoyang, sending off and receiving the dwelling—without shame before Zhou and Huo; receiving the testament he became assistant; far and near were settled.
translations.idiomatic: From Wan to Luoyang he sent off and received the dwelling without shame before Zhou and Huo; taking the testament he assisted until far and near were calm.

sentences.zh: 分陝恒方，流詠燕趙；

translations.literal: Dividing Shaan and Heng regions, his praise flowed in Yan and Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: Holding Shaan and Heng, praise flowed through Yan and Zhao;

sentences.zh: 廓靖江西，威懾南越。

translations.literal: pacifying and quieting west of the river, his awe subdued the southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: pacifying the west of the river, his awe subdued the southern Yue.

sentences.zh: 入釐百揆，庶績咸熙，履勤不憚，在功愈挹。

translations.literal: Entering to adjust the hundred duties, all achievements were bright; diligent in toil he did not weary; in merit he only grew more modest.
translations.idiomatic: Adjusting the hundred duties, all achievements bright; tireless in toil, in merit he only grew more modest.

sentences.zh: 溫恭愷悌，忠雅寬仁，興居有度，善終篤始。

translations.literal: Warm, respectful, harmonious, and kind; loyal, refined, and broad in benevolence; rising and dwelling had measure; he ended well because he began with depth.
translations.idiomatic: Warm, respectful, harmonious, and kind; loyal, refined, and broad; measured in rising and dwelling; he ended as deeply as he began.

sentences.zh: 高尚厥心，功成身退。

translations.literal: Lofty was his heart; merit complete, his person withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty in heart; merit complete, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 義亮聖衷，美光世典。

translations.literal: Righteousness brightened the sage breast; beauty lit the age's canon.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness lit the sage breast; beauty lit the age's canon.

sentences.zh: 依諡法，保大定功曰『武』，善問周達曰『宣』，諡曰武宣王。

translations.literal: According to the posthumous law, preserving the great and settling merit is called "Martial"; good inquiry reaching everywhere is called "Proclaimer"; posthumous name: Prince Martial-Proclaimer.
translations.idiomatic: By posthumous law, preserving the great and settling merit is Martial, good inquiry everywhere is Proclaimer—the posthumous name Prince Martial-Proclaimer.

sentences.zh: 」及莊帝即位，追號文穆皇帝，妃李氏為文穆皇后，遷神主於太廟，廟稱肅祖。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, he was posthumously titled Emperor Wenmu; consort Lady Li was Empress Wenmu; the spirit tablet was moved to the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the temple name was Sizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangdi took the throne he was posthumously Emperor Wenmu and Lady Li Empress Wenmu; the tablet entered the ancestral temple as Sizu.

sentences.zh: 語在臨淮王彧傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Prince Yu of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: The account is in the biography of Prince Yu of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝時，去其神主。

translations.literal: In the time of the Former Deposed Emperor, his spirit tablet was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Former Deposed Emperor his tablet was removed.

sentences.zh: 韶字世冑，襲。

translations.literal: Shao, styled Shizhou, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, styled Shizhou, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武定末，司州牧。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Si Province governor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was Si Province governor.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, his title was lowered per precedent.

sentences.zh: 韶弟襲，字世紹。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Xi, styled Shishao.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's younger brother Xi, styled Shishao.

sentences.zh: 武定初，封武安王，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was enfeoffed Prince of Wu'an, fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuding he was made Prince of Wu'an with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 武定末，中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, his title was lowered per precedent.

sentences.zh: 劭兄子直，字方言。

translations.literal: Shao's elder brother's son Zhi, styled Fangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's nephew Zhi, styled Fangyan.

sentences.zh: 少知名，為清河文獻王所賞愛。

translations.literal: From youth he was known by name; the Literary Prince of Qinghe prized and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Known from youth, he was prized by the Literary Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 起家除散騎侍郎，轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the start of his career he was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He began as regular attendant of scattered cavalry, then secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後除通直散騎常侍，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was regular attendant of direct communication, then gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 靈太后詔曰：「故太師、彭城武宣王道隆德盛，功高微管，協契先朝，導揚末命。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling's edict said: "The late Grand Preceptor, Prince Martial-Proclaimer of Pengcheng—his Way was lofty, his virtue abundant; merit surpassed Weiguan; he matched the former court and guided the last charge."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling wrote: "The late grand preceptor, Prince Martial-Proclaimer of Pengcheng—Way lofty, virtue abundant, merit past Weiguan, matched the former court and guided the last charge."

sentences.zh: 扶痾濟難，效漢北之誠；

translations.literal: "Supporting illness and rescuing difficulty, he showed the loyalty of north of Han;"
translations.idiomatic: "Supporting illness and rescuing trouble, he showed loyalty north of Han;"

sentences.zh: 送往奉居，盡魯南之節。

translations.literal: "sending off and receiving the dwelling, he fulfilled the integrity of south of Lu."
translations.idiomatic: "sending off and receiving the dwelling, he fulfilled the integrity south of Lu."

sentences.zh: 宗社賴之以安，皇基由之永固。

translations.literal: "The altars relied on him for peace; the imperial foundation by him was forever firm."
translations.idiomatic: "The altars leaned on him; the throne stood firm by him."

sentences.zh: 而謙光守約，屢撝增邑之賞；

translations.literal: "Yet humble light and keeping to covenant, he repeatedly waved off added fief rewards;"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet humble and keeping covenant, he waved off added fiefs;"

sentences.zh: 辭多受少，終保初錫之封。

translations.literal: "declining much and accepting little, he finally kept the first grant's seal."
translations.idiomatic: "declining much and taking little, he kept the first grant."

sentences.zh: 非所謂追舊報恩、念勳酬德者也。

translations.literal: "This is not what is called pursuing the old to repay kindness and remembering merit to repay virtue."
translations.idiomatic: "That is not pursuing the old to repay kindness or remembering merit to repay virtue."

sentences.zh: 可以前後所封戶，別封三子為縣公，食邑各一千戶，庶以少慰仁魂，微申朝典。

translations.literal: "From the households enfeoffed before and after, separately enfeoff three sons as county dukes, each with a fief of one thousand households, hoping in small measure to comfort the benevolent soul and slightly declare the court's canon."
translations.idiomatic: "From fiefs given before and after, enfeoff three sons as county dukes of a thousand households each, to comfort his soul and slightly declare the court's canon."

sentences.zh: 」子直封真定縣開國公。

translations.literal: Son Zhi was enfeoffed Duke of Zhending with an open state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was enfeoffed Duke of Zhending with an open state.

sentences.zh: 出為冠軍將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Champion General and Liang Province inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as champion general and Liang inspector.

sentences.zh: 未幾遇患，優遊南鄭，無他政績。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill; he lingered at ease in Nanzheng without other achievement in government.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill and lingered at ease in Nanzheng without other achievement.

sentences.zh: 徵還京師，病卒。

translations.literal: Summoned back to the capital, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、安南將軍、都官尚書、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously: Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the South, Director of the Ministry of Justice, Ji Province inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously: regular attendant of scattered cavalry, general who pacifies the south, director of the ministry of justice, and Ji inspector.

sentences.zh: 孝莊踐阼，追封陳留王，邑二千戶，贈假黃鉞、太師、大司馬、太尉，加前後部羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhuang took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu, fief of two thousand households, given Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, Grand Commandant, and front and rear feathered canopy and drum escort.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozhuang's accession he was posthumously Prince of Chenliu with two thousand households, acting yellow battle-ax, grand preceptor, grand marshal, and grand commandant, with feathered escort.

sentences.zh: 子寬，字思猛，襲王爵。

translations.literal: Son Kuan, styled Simeng, inherited the princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: Son Kuan, styled Simeng, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 除散騎常侍、平南將軍。

translations.literal: He was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was regular attendant of scattered cavalry and general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中、撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was palace attendant and general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，尒朱兆害之於晉陽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an, Erzhu Zhao killed him at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an year 3 Erzhu Zhao killed him at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 無後，國除。

translations.literal: He had no heir; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He had no heir; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，追贈使持節、散騎常侍、都督青齊濟三州諸軍事、衞大將軍、青州刺史，重贈司徒公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Commander of military affairs in Qing, Qi, and Ji provinces, Defender Grand General, Qing Province inspector; again posthumously Duke Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: At the Deposed Emperor's accession he was posthumously bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry attendant, commander of Qing, Qi, and Ji, defender grand general, and Qing inspector, then again duke minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 弟剛，字金明。

translations.literal: Younger brother Gang, styled Jinming.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Gang, styled Jinming.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，封浮陽王，邑千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Fuyang, fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuangdi's accession he was Prince of Fuyang with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 武定末，宗正少卿。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was vice director of the imperial clan court.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, his title was lowered per precedent.

sentences.zh: 剛弟質，莊帝初，林慮王，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Gang's younger brother Zhi; at the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign, Prince of Linyu, fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Gang's younger brother Zhi was Prince of Linyu at Zhuangdi's accession, with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 永安三年薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yong'an year 3.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，贈車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the Deposed Emperor's time he was posthumously given General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Protocol of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor he was posthumously general of chariots and cavalry, left grand master of splendid happiness, and protocol of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 劭弟子正，美貌，性寬和。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother's son Zheng was handsome in appearance and by nature mild and broad.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's nephew Zheng was handsome and mild by nature.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，封霸城縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he was enfeoffed Duke of Bacheng, fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzong's accession he was Duke of Bacheng with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 歷散騎侍郎、太常少卿。

translations.literal: He served as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served as scattered-cavalry attendant and vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，除尚書令，封始平王。

translations.literal: When Zhuangdi took the throne he was made Minister over the Masses and enfeoffed Prince of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuangdi's accession he was minister over the masses and Prince of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 與兄劭俱遇害。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Shao both met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Shao both met disaster.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、錄尚書事、相，[5]王如故，鸞輅九旒、黃屋左纛、前後部羽葆鼓吹、虎賁班劍一百人，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, Grand General, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Xiang [5]—Prince as before; imperial carriage with nine tassels, yellow canopy with left streamer, front and rear feathered canopy and drum escort, a hundred tiger guards with swords of state; posthumous name: Upright.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously: acting yellow battle-ax, palace attendant, commander of all armies, grand general, recorder of the Masters of Writing, Xiang [5], prince as before; nine-tassel carriage, yellow canopy with left streamer, feathered escort, a hundred tiger guards; posthumous name Upright.

sentences.zh: 子欽，字世道，襲。

translations.literal: Son Qin, styled Shidao, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Qin, styled Shidao, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武定中，散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In Wuding he was Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuding he was scattered-cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, his title was lowered per precedent.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：武宣王孝以為質，忠而樹行，文謀武略，自得懷抱，綢繆太和之世，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: The historian says: Prince Martial-Proclaimer took filial piety as his substance and planted conduct with loyalty; literary stratagem and martial strategy came from his own breast; in the Taihe era he was bound close—was it in vain!
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Prince Martial-Proclaimer made filial piety his substance and loyalty his conduct; literary and martial strategy came from his own breast; in the Taihe years he was bound close—not in vain.

sentences.zh: 至夫在安處危之操，送往事居之節，周旦匪他之義，霍光異姓之誠，事兼之矣。

translations.literal: As for conduct in safety yet facing danger, integrity in sending off the past and dwelling in the present, the righteousness of the Duke of Zhou not being another, the loyalty of Huo Guang as a different surname—the affairs were combined in him.
translations.idiomatic: Conduct safe in danger, integrity in sending off the past and dwelling in the present, Zhou's righteousness not being another's, Huo's loyalty though of different surname—all combined in him.

sentences.zh: 功高震主，德隆動俗，間言一入，卒不全志。

translations.literal: Merit high enough to shake the ruler, virtue lofty enough to move custom—one slander entered, and in the end his will was not preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Merit that shook the throne, virtue that moved custom—one whisper entered, and his will was not preserved.

sentences.zh: 烏呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 周成、漢昭亦未易遇也。

translations.literal: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Zhao of Han were likewise not easy to encounter.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Zhou of King Cheng or the Han of Emperor Zhao was scarcely met with again.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Textual collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 但汝以我親 諸本「以我親」作「亦我」二字。

translations.literal: "But you take me as kin": in various editions the two characters "yi wo qin" (take me as kin) appear as the two characters "yi wo" (also me).
translations.idiomatic: "But you take me as kin": editions read yi wo qin (take me as kin) as the two characters yi wo (also me).

sentences.zh: 冊府卷二八六宋本如上摘句，明本

translations.literal: Cefu yuangu juan 286, Song edition as quoted above; Ming edition
translations.idiomatic: Cefu juan 286, Song edition as above; Ming edition

sentences.zh: 〈三三六五頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3365〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 3365

sentences.zh: 作「以親」二字。

translations.literal: reads the two characters "yi qin" (as kin).
translations.idiomatic: has "yi qin" (as kin).

sentences.zh: 按「但汝亦我」語不可解，顯誤，今據宋本冊府改補。

translations.literal: Commentary: The phrase "but you also me" is unintelligible and clearly erroneous; now emended and supplied according to the Song edition of Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "but you also me" makes no sense and is clearly corrupt; the text is emended per the Song Cefu.

sentences.zh: 比鳳皇未至 諸本「至」作「一」，下注「疑」字，今據冊府卷二六九

translations.literal: "Compared to the phoenix not yet arriving": in various editions "zhi" (arrive) is written as "yi" (one), with the note below "suspected"; now according to Cefu juan 269
translations.idiomatic: "Compared to the phoenix not yet arriving": editions read zhi (arrive) as yi (one), with yi (suspect) in the note below; emended per Cefu juan 269

sentences.zh: 〈三一八四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3184〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 3184

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: Corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Emended.

sentences.zh: 以其舅潘僧固為冀州樂陵太守 北史卷一九彭城王勰傳「樂陵」作「長樂」。

translations.literal: "Appointed his maternal uncle Pan Senggu as Administrator of Leling in Ji Province": in Beishi juan 19, Biography of Prince of Pengcheng Xie, "Leling" is written as "Changle."
translations.idiomatic: "Appointed his maternal uncle Pan Senggu Administrator of Leling, Ji Province": Beishi juan 19 (Pengcheng Wang Xie) reads Leling as Changle.

sentences.zh: 按冀州有長樂，無樂陵，樂陵屬青州，見卷一０六地形志上及中。

translations.literal: Commentary: Ji Province has Changle but not Leling; Leling belongs to Qing Province—see juan 106, Monograph on Geography, upper and middle.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Ji had Changle but not Leling; Leling was in Qing—Geography monograph juan 106, upper and middle.

sentences.zh: 此傳當誤。

translations.literal: This biography ought to be erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: The life is in error.

sentences.zh: 于時齊州民劉均房頃等扇動三齊蕭衍遣將彭群王辯等搔擾邊陲 卷九肅宗紀孝昌三年三月「房頃」作「房須」，參卷九校記[二０]。

translations.literal: "At that time the people of Qi Province, Liu Jun, Fang Qing, and others, stirred up the Three Qi; Xiao Yan sent generals Peng Qun, Wang Bian, and others to harass the frontier": in juan 9, Annals of Emperor Suzong, third month of the third year of Xiaochang, "Fang Qing" is written as "Fang Xu"; see collation note [20] to juan 9.
translations.idiomatic: "At that time Qi people Liu Jun, Fang Qing, and others stirred the Three Qi; Xiao Yan sent Peng Qun, Wang Bian, and others to trouble the border": Suzong annals juan 9, Xiaochang year 3 month 3 reads Fang Qing as Fang Xu—see juan 9 collation note [20].

sentences.zh: 又諸本「彭」下有「城」字，「群」作「郡」。

translations.literal: Moreover in various editions below "Peng" there is the character "cheng" (city), and "qun" (cluster) is written as "jun" (commandery).
translations.idiomatic: Editions also add cheng (city) after Peng and read qun (cluster) as jun (commandery).

sentences.zh: 按卷九肅宗紀孝昌三年正月、卷七九鹿悆傳、冊府卷一二一

translations.literal: Commentary: juan 9, Annals of Emperor Suzong, first month of the third year of Xiaochang; juan 79, Biography of Lu Yu; Cefu juan 121
translations.idiomatic: Note: Suzong annals juan 9, Xiaochang year 3 month 1; Lu Yu biography juan 79; Cefu juan 121

sentences.zh: 〈一四五一頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 1451〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 1451

sentences.zh: 均作「彭群、王辯」，彭群是人名。

translations.literal: all read "Peng Qun, Wang Bian"; Peng Qun is a personal name.
translations.idiomatic: all have "Peng Qun, Wang Bian"—Peng Qun is a man's name.

sentences.zh: 這裏「群」訛「郡」，後人又妄加「城」字。

translations.literal: Here "qun" (cluster) is corrupted as "jun" (commandery), and later people additionally inserted the character "cheng" (city) without basis.
translations.idiomatic: Here qun (cluster) was miscopied as jun (commandery), and later scribes spuriously added cheng (city).

sentences.zh: 今據刪正。

translations.literal: Now according to this, deleted and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The text is now trimmed and emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書事相 按「相」上當脫「丞」字，或「相」下脫「國」字。

translations.literal: "Director of the Masters of Writing, minister": Commentary: above "xiang" (minister) the character "cheng" (director) has probably dropped, or below "xiang" the character "guo" (state) has dropped.
translations.idiomatic: "Director of the Masters of Writing, minister": Note: cheng (director) may be missing before xiang (minister), or guo (state) after xiang.
